jobs.title: Lead AI Engineer (m/w/d) – Remote
jobs.description:
Worum es geht

MAIA ist eine KI-Plattform für Unternehmen. Mit MAIA durchsuchen Teams ihre internen Daten und verankern Agenten tief in ihren Prozessen. Wir begleiten Unternehmen dabei, KI nicht nur in einzelnen Abteilungen, sondern im ganzen Unternehmen einzusetzen.

Technisch heißt das: Wir bauen eine GenAI-Anwendung mit eigenen Agentensystemen, RAG-Pipelines und agentenbasierten Workflows, binden externe Systeme unserer Kunden an und analysieren ihre Daten. Wir nutzen die besten verfügbaren Modelle, betrieben in der EU, und machen sie verlässlich für anspruchsvolle Arbeit mit großen, komplexen Datenmengen.

Zahlreiche Industrieunternehmen arbeiten seit Jahren intensiv mit MAIA. Nach unserer erfolgreichen Finanzierungsrunde 2026 bringen wir MAIA jetzt in die Breite. Entwickelt wird MAIA seit 2021 in Leipzig.

Was du bei uns machst

Als Lead AI Engineer führst du unser Engineering-Team, entwickelst rund drei Viertel deiner Zeit selbst mit und arbeitest eng mit unserem CTO zusammen.

Deine Schwerpunkte:

  • Selbst entwickeln. Du übernimmst anspruchsvolle Features und Architekturthemen in unseren Agenten-, RAG- und Workflow-Systemen und schreibst Pläne, an denen sich andere orientieren.

  • Technische Richtung. Du triffst wichtige Designentscheidungen mit, priorisierst gemeinsam mit dem CTO die technische Roadmap und treibst die technische Vision von MAIA voran.

  • Das Team anführen. Du koordinierst die Arbeit im Team und bist Sparringspartner für alle Engineers, in Designdiskussionen, Reviews und Feedback. Du führst technische Interviews und entscheidest mit, wen wir einstellen.

  • Besser werden, gemeinsam. Mit dem Team verbesserst du laufend, wie wir entwickeln, gerade im agentischen Arbeiten: von Plänen und Reviews über Evals bis zu Releases.

  • Am Puls der Technik. Du verfolgst neue Entwicklungen bei LLMs, Retrieval, Agenten und darüber hinaus, bewertest sie nüchtern und bringst ins Produkt, was trägt.

Was wir suchen

  • Ein herausragender AI Engineer. Du hast LLM-Systeme gebaut und in Produktion betrieben. RAG, Embeddings, Vektorsuche, Tool Calling und Agenten kennst du aus der Praxis, auch die Stellen, an denen sie scheitern. Neue Modelle und Techniken probierst du aus eigenem Antrieb aus und trennst dabei Substanz von Hype.

  • Starke Architektur. Du hast Backend-Systeme gebaut, ausgeliefert und über längere Zeit in Produktion betrieben. Du triffst Designentscheidungen, die auch in einem Jahr noch tragen, und erkennst schwache Architektur auch dann, wenn ein Coding Agent sie geschrieben hat.

  • Sehr gut in mindestens einer unserer Sprachen. TypeScript, Python oder Go, am besten eine der statisch typisierten. Alle drei musst du nicht mitbringen. In die anderen arbeitest du dich ein.

  • Technische Führung. Du hast ein Team als Tech Lead, Lead Engineer oder in einer vergleichbaren Rolle fachlich geführt. Wie die Rolle hieß, ist zweitrangig. Du gibst Verantwortung ab und freust dich, wenn das Team ohne dich gute Entscheidungen trifft. Gleichzeitig entwickelst du gern selbst weiter, denn diese Rolle ist keine reine Managementrolle.

  • Messen statt vermuten. Du weißt, wie man Systeme testet und evaluiert, die auf dieselbe Frage nicht immer gleich antworten. Du baust die einfachste Lösung, die das Problem löst. Weitere Retrieval-Stufen, Prompt-Ketten oder Abstraktionen kommen erst dazu, wenn Messungen sie rechtfertigen.

  • Agentisch arbeiten. Coding Agents gehören für dich zum Alltag. Du hast eine klare Meinung dazu, wie ein Team mit ihnen schnell bleibt, ohne an Qualität zu verlieren.

  • Remote führen. Du führst auch aus der Ferne wirksam. Du kommunizierst proaktiv, machst Entscheidungen schriftlich nachvollziehbar und bist für das Team gut erreichbar.

  • Sicherheit mitdenken. Unsere Kunden vertrauen uns ihr internes Wissen an. Mandantentrennung, Zugriffsrechte und sichere Entwicklung sind für dich selbstverständlich.

  • Klar kommunizieren. Du sprichst Probleme früh an, argumentierst mit Belegen und erklärst technische Entscheidungen verständlich, im Team ebenso wie gegenüber Produktmanagement, Customer Success und Vertrieb. Du sprichst sehr sicher Deutsch und ebenso Englisch.

Arbeiten bei MAIA

Uns verbindet ein gemeinsames Ziel: ein richtig gutes Produkt zu bauen. Jede und jeder übernimmt Verantwortung für das eigene Thema. Wir haben Spaß an der Arbeit und sind stolz auf das, was unsere Kunden mit MAIA erreichen. Die Wege sind kurz, und Entscheidungen fallen schnell. Im Engineering-Team hinterfragen wir kritisch, wie wir entwickeln, und verbessern unsere Prozesse laufend, gerade in der agentischen Entwicklung.

Ein großer Teil des Teams arbeitet gemeinsam in unserem Büro in Leipzig, zentral zwischen Innenstadt und Zoo, und kocht fast jeden Tag zusammen. Du arbeitest remote von überall in Deutschland, dein Wohnsitz muss in Deutschland liegen. Zweimal im Jahr treffen wir uns zu Team-Events, und ab und zu gibt es Teamtage in Leipzig. Wann dein Tag beginnt, legst du selbst fest.

  • Zugang zu aktuellen Frontier-Modellen und Coding Agents

  • Unterstützung bei Weiterbildungen, auch zu Führungsthemen

  • Zugang zu einer Wellpass-Mitgliedschaft

Vergütung

Das Jahresbruttogehalt liegt bei 90.000 bis 100.000 €. Wo du in dieser Spanne liegst, besprechen wir spätestens nach dem Interview zu Technik und Führung. Dazu kommt eine virtuelle Beteiligung über unser VSOP.

Bewerbung und nächste Schritte

Ein Anschreiben brauchst du nicht. Schick uns deinen Lebenslauf und beantworte uns in ein paar eigenen Sätzen eine Frage: Warum willst du MAIA mitgestalten?

Wir arbeiten jeden Tag mit KI. Für diese Antwort zählt aber deine eigene Perspektive. Schreib sie deshalb bitte selbst, gern kurz und ohne Feinschliff.

Passt es, folgen ein 30-minütiges Kennenlernen, ein 90-minütiges Interview zu Technik und Führung und ein Abschlussgespräch mit der Geschäftsführung. Nach jedem Schritt hörst du in der Regel innerhalb von zwei Werktagen von uns. Unser Ziel ist eine Entscheidung in rund drei Wochen.

Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung.

jobs.title: (Senior) Product Engineer – AI (m/f/d) – Remote
jobs.description:
What we do

MAIA is an AI platform for companies. With MAIA, teams search their internal data and embed agents deep into their processes. We help companies use AI not just in individual departments, but across the entire organisation.

On a technical level, this means: we build a GenAI application with our own agent systems, RAG pipelines and agent-based workflows, connect our customers' external systems and analyse their data. We use the best available models, operated in the EU, and make them reliable for demanding work with large, complex datasets.

Many industrial companies have been using MAIA intensively for years. Following our successful 2026 funding round, we are now taking MAIA to a broader market. MAIA has been developed in Leipzig since 2021.

What you'll do

As a Product Engineer, you own features from start to finish: from conversations with customers and concept work through to implementation and continuous improvement in production.

What you can work on:

  • Understanding customers and the market. You talk to users, join customer meetings and analyse usage data. This way, you find out where MAIA can help most in people's daily work. You work closely with product management and customer success.

  • From problem to concept. You write concepts, build prototypes to test ideas quickly, and slice features so they reach users early.

  • Building across the full stack. You write the implementation plan, let coding agents implement it, and own architecture and quality, from the data model to the user interface.

  • AI that people understand. You shape how people work with MAIA: asking questions, providing context, letting agents complete multi-step tasks and following their results.

  • Measuring and improving. After a release, you check whether a feature is used and actually helps, and you keep improving it based on feedback, usage data and evals.

What we're looking for

  • Solid software engineering. You have built products that people use every day and operated them in production, across backend and frontend. You recognise weak architecture even when a coding agent wrote it.

  • Very strong in at least one of our languages. TypeScript, Python or Go, ideally one of the statically typed ones. You don't need all three. You'll get up to speed in the others.

  • Product experience. You have talked to customers, questioned requirements and taken features from the first idea to daily use. You listen closely and recognise the problem behind a request.

  • A feel for good usability. You notice when an interface overwhelms people, and you'd rather build a simple solution that people understand than a powerful one that nobody finds.

  • At home in the LLM ecosystem. You have built applications with LLMs, professionally or in complex personal projects, and you know their quirks: answers vary, take time, and agents fail in unexpected places. You build products that deal with this honestly.

  • Measure, don't guess. You check whether a feature works using usage data, feedback and evals. You build the simplest solution that solves the problem.

  • Agentic engineering. Coding agents are part of your daily work. You write plans that others review and that coding agents can build on, you review the results critically, and you know where agents help and where they don't.

  • Remote-ready. You communicate proactively, document your work so others can follow it, and move things forward without constant coordination.

  • Clear communication. People understand your concepts on first read. You enjoy talking to customers as much as to engineers. You are fluent in English. German is a strong plus, as many of our customer conversations are in German.

This role has no people management responsibility. Whether you join at regular or senior level is something we'll discuss openly with you after the technical interview at the latest.

Working at MAIA

We share a common goal: building a really great product. Everyone takes ownership of their own area. We enjoy our work and are proud of what our customers achieve with MAIA. Paths are short and decisions are made quickly. In the engineering team, we critically question how we develop and continuously improve our processes, especially in agentic development.

Much of the team works together in our office in Leipzig, centrally located between the city centre and the zoo, where we cook together almost every day. You work remotely from anywhere in Germany. You need to live in Germany for this role. Twice a year, we meet in person for team events, and from time to time there are team days in Leipzig. When your day starts is up to you.

  • Access to the latest frontier models and coding agents

  • Support for training that fits your professional development

  • Access to a Wellpass membership

Compensation

The annual gross salary is €75,000 to €95,000. Where you fall within this range depends on your level. We'll discuss this after the technical interview at the latest. On top of that, you receive a virtual share in our VSOP.

Application and next steps

You don't need a cover letter. Send us your CV and answer one question in a few sentences of your own: Why do you want to help shape MAIA?

We work with AI every day. For this answer, though, your own perspective is what counts. So please write it yourself. Short and unpolished is fine.

If there's a fit, you'll have a 30-minute intro call, a 90-minute technical interview that also covers product decisions and a final conversation with our management. After each step, you'll usually hear from us within two business days. Our goal is a decision in about three weeks.

We look forward to your application.

You will engage with C-level executives and Legal Operations leaders to position our industry-leading SaaS solutions, ensuring we address the critical needs of modern legal departments.

Required Skills:

  • Experience: 5 years of SaaS enterprise sales experience, with a consistent track record of exceeding quotas. 
  • Fortune 500 Expertise: Demonstrated success selling to and winning business from Fortune 500 companies. 
  • New Logo Focus: Exceptional experience driving new customer acquisition, not just account expansion. 
  • Legal Ops Knowledge: Strong understanding of Legal Operations functions, challenges, technology landscape, and emerging trends including legal technology, contract lifecycle management (CLM), e-discovery, and corporate compliance software. Experience collaborating with Legal Operations professional groups (e.g., CLOC, ACC) 
  • Sales Acumen: Proficiency in solution selling methodologies (e.g., MEDDIC, Challenger Sale, SPIN Selling) and complex deal management. 
  • Executive Presence: Ability to credibly engage with and sell to General Counsel, Chief Legal Officers, and other C-level executives. Strong presentation skills with the ability to simplify complex technology into compelling business outcomes

  • Tools: Proficiency in CRM systems (Salesforce preferred), LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Outreach and other sales productivity tools. 
  • Education: Bachelor's degree preferred.

Benefits & Perks That Support You:

Onit offers a comprehensive total rewards package designed to support the whole employee at work and beyond:
Health Coverage Choices: Three medical plan options, plus dental and vision, so you can choose what fits best. Employees on our HDHP plan also receive employer contribution to the HSA.
Retirement Savings: 401(k) with a 100% match on the first 3% and 50% on the next 2% of employee contributions.
Time Away: Flexible paid time off, 7 sick days, and 9 paid company holidays annually.
Family Support: Exceptional paid leave for birth parents, non-birth parents, and caregivers. Onit also offers surrogacy and adoption reimbursement.
Income Protection: 100% employer-paid life and disability insurance.
Additional Coverage Options: Voluntary benefits including hospital indemnity, critical illness, accident, and even pet insurance.
Tax-Advantaged Accounts: Healthcare FSA, HSA, and dependent care FSA.
Community Engagement: One paid volunteer day each year to give back to the community.

Our Commitment to Applicants

We know that not everyone will check every box in a job description. At Onit, we value diversity, inclusion, and authenticity. If you’re excited about this role but your experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification, we encourage you to apply. You may be exactly who we’re looking for.

Program: Army Global Unified Network (AGUN)

Help Ensure Quality Across the U.S. Army's Global Network!

Leidos is seeking a detail-oriented Quality & Acceptance Coordinator to support the Army Global Unified Network (AGUN) program.

In this role, you'll help ensure network installations meet technical, quality, and contractual requirements before they are submitted for Government acceptance.

You'll work with engineering, deployment, logistics, and subcontractor teams to coordinate inspections, review technical documentation, track corrective actions, and support successful project closeout.

jobs.title: Marketing Ops Manager I
jobs.description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role

We're looking for a technically strong, forward-thinking specialist to help shape the next generation of Campaign Operations. This role focuses on innovation, AI-driven capabilities, and technical solutions that make our campaign operating model more intelligent, scalable, and efficient.

You'll spend most of your time designing and building: prototyping AI agents, automations, and integrations, then turning the ones that work into reusable capabilities the whole team can adopt. You'll also bring enough Campaign Operations expertise to support campaign execution when needed.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won't be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
  • You're energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-calibre team that will encourage you to do your best.

In this role, you will:

  • Drive innovation: Explore emerging technologies, identify opportunities, and build next-generation Campaign Operations capabilities that go beyond traditional automation.
  • Build AI and technical solutions: Design, prototype, and implement solutions using AI agents, automation, APIs, and scripting, taking scoped projects from concept through implementation.
  • Own internal tools and agents: Maintain and improve the team's intake agent and other internal tools, including issue triage, stakeholder feedback, and a roadmap for what comes next.
  • Optimize operations: Find opportunities to improve scalability, efficiency, quality, and reliability across campaign workflows and systems, and measure the impact.
  • Lead cross-functional technical initiatives: Serve as the Campaign Operations point person for platform and workflow projects, such as marketing automation platform migrations, owning project plans, timelines, and stakeholder alignment while partnering with MarTech, MDA, Web Dev, Engineering, and vendor teams.
  • Own shared processes: Document, standardize, and automate capabilities such as list uploads and landing-page creation, building repeatable processes and clarifying dependencies with partner teams.
  • Shape the technical roadmap: Help shape and own the technical and AI roadmap for Campaign Operations: decide which capabilities to bring in-house, integrate, rebuild, or automate, and serve as the Campaign Ops subject matter expert and owner for the semantic layer and standardized skills that power our agentic workflows.
  • Provide lead flow backup coverage: Act as a backup point of contact for critical lead flow outages and technical troubleshooting (e.g., audit logs, vendor support), in partnership with the lead flow owners.
  • Enable the team: Share knowledge, drive adoption of new capabilities, and provide hands-on campaign execution support when needed.
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices.

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 7+ years of hands-on campaign operations experience at a fast-paced B2B technology company, including hands-on execution of multi-channel campaigns (email, landing pages, webinars) in a marketing automation platform such as Marketo, Iterable, and/or HubSpot.
  • Proficiency building AI agents and automated workflows with tools like Claude Code, Cursor, Gumloop, n8n, or similar.
  • Proficiency in Python or JavaScript, plus working experience with APIs, integrations, and data manipulation.
  • Experience experimenting with emerging technologies and turning concepts into functional, maintainable solutions.
  • Strong project management and process orientation: able to scope, plan, and drive cross-functional initiatives from intake to delivery, and to document and standardize repeatable processes.
  • Strong analytical thinking, problem-solving skills, curiosity, and a builder mindset.
  • Ability to work independently, collaborate cross-functionally, and adapt quickly in a fast-paced environment.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate operational needs into practical technical solutions.

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Experience with Marketo and/or Iterable.
  • Familiarity with AI-native or AI-forward marketing automation platforms, and experience evaluating or migrating between MAPs.
  • Experience with SQL, Salesforce, Hightouch, Databricks, Airtable, Zapier, Workato, or Splash.
  • General marketing operations exposure to lead flow concepts such as routing, scoring, and lifecycle stages.
  • Familiarity with MCP, agent frameworks (e.g., LangChain), and semantic-layer concepts for agentic workflows.
  • Familiarity with email compliance regulations (e.g., GDPR, CAN-SPAM, CASL) and data privacy best practices.
  • Basic familiarity with HTML and CSS.

The compensation range shown spans approved pay zones for this role. Your primary work location determines the range applicable to you, which may be narrower than the full range displayed.

The range of annual base salary for full-time employees for this position is below. Please note that base pay offered may vary depending on factors including your city of residence, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. This role is also eligible for an initial RSU grant with no vesting cliff, and ongoing refresh opportunities tied to performance, subject to plan terms and conditions. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

Annual Base Salary
$113,050—$146,300 CAD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co. For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our blog post here.

jobs.title: Miltary Spouse Employer Partnership (MSEP) Program Manager (PM)
jobs.description:
The Health and Services Sector/Behavioral Health and Readiness Business Area at Leidos currently has an opening for a SpouseWorks MSEP PM to work in the Washington, D.C., Maryland, and Northern Virginia (DMV) area. This is an exciting opportunity to support the Department of War SpouseWorks mission: helping military spouses pursue meaningful, sustainable careers despite frequent relocations, employment interruptions, and other challenges of military life.


MSEP (Military Spouse Employer Partnership) connects military spouses with participating employers, including businesses, federal agencies, and nonprofit organizations, to expand access to employment opportunities. Through the MSEP employer-partner network and job-search resources, the initiative helps employers access military spouse talent while supporting spouses in finding jobs aligned with their skills and career goals. The MSEP PM will lead a nationwide employer-partnership operation supporting a portfolio of more than 1,200 partners, strengthening existing relationships while expanding the network and increasing meaningful hiring opportunities.


The MSEP PM is responsible for daily execution, employer recruitment and engagement, workforce leadership, Government coordination, performance reporting, outreach, and continuous improvement. Success means not only adding partners, but helping convert employer commitments into documented employment opportunities and military spouse hires.


Primary Responsibilities

  • Program Leadership and Government Coordination. Lead day-to-day MSEP operations and contractual deliverables; serve as a principal MSEP point of contact for Government stakeholders; develop execution plans, priorities, schedules, and corrective actions aligned with SpouseWorks objectives.
  • Employer-Partner Recruitment and Growth. Develop and execute a targeted national strategy to identify, qualify, recruit, onboard, and expand employer partnerships across industries, including corporations, small businesses, federal agencies, and nonprofit organizations. Prioritize employers offering viable career pathways for military spouses.
  • Partner Engagement and Retention. Direct ongoing partner relationship management; establish engagement plans, monitor participation, reengage inactive partners, and strengthen employers’ understanding of military spouse talent and the business value of hiring military spouses.
  • Military Spouse Hiring Outcomes. Work with partners to increase relevant job postings, recruiting events, referrals, interviews, and hires; encourage timely, consistent reporting of military spouse hiring outcomes; identify gaps between partner participation and actual hiring activity.
  • Workforce Management. Lead, supervise, train, coach, and evaluate geographically dispersed MSEP recruiters, partner specialists/account managers, and operational support personnel; assign workloads and establish consistent processes and performance expectations.
  • Partner Lifecycle and Quality Assurance. Oversee prospect qualification, application review, partner vetting, Government approval coordination, onboarding, orientation webinars, partner support, and periodic relationship reviews; maintain accurate records and consistent handoffs.

Descrizione del lavoro:

The Director, Global Sales – Personal Care leads the worldwide sales strategy and execution for BW Converting's personal care product lines within the Hygiene segment. This leader is accountable for order intake, market share growth and margin performance for converting equipment, used to produce baby care, feminine care, adult care and wet wipes products.

Personal care is a developing product line with significant growth potential. The Director will rebuild and energize the personal care sales organization, open doors with new customers and regions, and bring a modern, consultative approach to selling complex capital equipment. In the near term, the role will also personally manage selected strategic accounts, including direct accounts.

The Director works closely with Product Management, Engineering, Project Management, Service and Operations to make sure customer needs, market opportunities and business objectives stay aligned, and champions Barry-Wehmiller's commitment to Truly Human Leadership.


Key Responsibilities

Personal Care Sales Strategy & Growth

  • Develop and execute the global sales strategy for personal care (baby care, feminine care, adult care and wet wipes) aligned with Hygiene segment objectives and growth plans.
  • Drive order intake, revenue growth, market share gains and margin improvement across all regions.
  • Identify target customers, segments and geographies, including multinational brand owners, private-label producers and emerging-market manufacturers.
  • Monitor market trends, competitor activity and customer needs, such as sustainability, product innovation, line flexibility and OEE, and translate them into sales priorities.
  • Contribute to the annual budget, sales forecast and long-range plan for the personal care business.

Sales Leadership & Team Development

  • Lead, coach and develop the global personal care sales team, including regional sales executives in Europe and North America.
  • Build a high-performing, accountable sales culture focused on new business development as well as growth with existing customers.
  • Establish consistent sales processes, pipeline management, forecasting discipline and key performance indicators.
  • Recruit and onboard new sales talent as the organization grows, and develop succession plans for key commercial roles.
  • Encourage collaboration with the Hygiene sales organizations in other product areas and regions to share customer relationships and best practices.
  • Built an agent/project finder network where appropriate.

Customer & Account Management

  • Personally manage selected strategic and key accounts, including direct accounts, and serve as executive sponsor for major opportunities.
  • Build trusted, long-term relationships with decision makers across engineering, operations, procurement and executive leadership at customer organizations.
  • Lead complex capital equipment sales cycles from opportunity identification through technical proposal, pricing, negotiation and contract award.
  • Partner with Project Management and Service to deliver a strong customer experience after the sale and to grow upgrade, retrofit and aftermarket business.
  • Represent BW Converting at customer meetings, industry conferences and trade shows such as IDEA and other hygiene and nonwovens events.

Commercial Excellence & Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner with Product Management and Engineering to shape the personal care portfolio, roadmap and new technology launches based on customer and market feedback.
  • Work with Engineering and customer-facing technical teams to prepare accurate, competitive proposals and solution concepts.
  • Apply value-based selling and pricing strategies that reflect total cost of ownership and the performance of BW Converting equipment.
  • Make effective use of CRM tools, market intelligence, and sales analytics to guide decisions and report results.
  • Provide regular, transparent reporting on pipeline, forecast, wins and losses to Hygiene segment leadership.

Leadership & Culture

  • Champion Barry-Wehmiller's Guiding Principles of Leadership and Truly Human Leadership by caring for team members while delivering business results.
  • Model integrity, respect and accountability in all customer and team interactions.
  • Foster a culture of continuous improvement, curiosity and customer focus within the commercial organization.

Qualifications & Experience

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Engineering, Marketing or a related field.
  • Minimum 10 years of progressive sales or commercial experience in capital equipment, industrial machinery, converting, packaging, nonwovens or related industries, including at least 3 years in a sales leadership role.
  • Proven track record of winning new customers and growing market share in a business-to-business capital equipment environment.
  • Strong experience managing complex, high-value sales cycles and negotiating with multinational customers.
  • Demonstrated success leading and developing sales teams across multiple countries and cultures.
  • Experience using CRM systems, pipeline management and forecasting tools.
  • Fluent English; additional European languages (such as German, Italian or Spanish) are a strong advantage.
  • Ability to travel internationally approximately 40–50% of the time.

Preferred

  • Direct experience selling converting equipment for absorbent hygiene products (baby diapers and pants, feminine care, adult incontinence or underpads).
  • Established network with personal care manufacturers in Europe, the Americas, the Middle East or Asia.
  • Experience working in a matrixed, global organization.

Leadership Competencies

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

  • Strategic thinking
  • Customer focus
  • Commercial acumen and negotiation skills
  • Business development and hunter mindset
  • Global and cross-cultural leadership
  • Change leadership
  • Talent development
  • Collaboration and partnership
  • Results orientation
  • Truly Human Leadership

jobs.title: Senior AI Platform Engineer (Tech Lead)
jobs.description:
This is a remote position.

About Us

Moring.ai builds enterprise AI that runs in production for regulated industries: financial services and other compliance-heavy organizations. We ship AI applications and agents inside our customers' own cloud environments, wired into the systems they already run. Not slideware, not demos.

We're early-stage, lean, and profitable, so what you ship reaches serious enterprises fast.

The Role

We are building an AI platform for a large financial services enterprise. It lets developers inside that organization build and deploy agentic AI workflows: Python applications that call LLMs, use tools, and run as agents on Kubernetes. The platform includes an LLM gateway, an agent runtime, MCP servers, a skills registry, retrieval, evals, observability, and governance.

We are hiring a Tech Lead to lead the engineers building it. You have 7–12 years of software engineering experience, and you are very strong on the software side: you write clean, well-tested Python, you design APIs and backend systems well, and you can go full stack when needed. You have a good working understanding of AI (agents, RAG, LLM applications) and you have built some of it hands-on, but the thing we are hiring you for is engineering: the hard problems in AI right now are reliability, cost, latency, security, and testing systems that don't give the same answer twice.

This is a highly hands-on lead role. You will write a large share of the code, review the rest, break the work down for the team, and keep the platform shippable. The architect sets the overall design; you make it real.

What You'll Do
  • Lead a team of 3–5 engineers: break down the work, set priorities with the architect and the CTO, review code, and keep delivery on track.
  • Write production code across the platform: the LLM gateway, the agent runtime, MCP servers, the skills and asset registry, evals, and the APIs developers use to deploy agents.
  • Design and build the APIs and services the platform exposes, in Python, with the habits of a production engineer: tests, observability, clean interfaces, clear error handling.
  • Build the developer-facing parts of the platform (CLI, SDK, or web UI) so an engineer at the customer can go from an idea to a deployed agent without asking us.
  • Own code quality: set the coding standards, the review process, the test strategy, and the CI/CD pipeline, and hold the team to them.
  • Build and extend the evaluation harness, so AI changes ship with evidence.
  • Deploy into the customer's environment: their AWS accounts, EKS clusters, private networks, and internal registries. Reproducible, with no manual steps.
  • Work with the customer's engineers in design sessions, demos, and security reviews.
  • Operate what the team builds: production ownership, on-call rotation, performance and cost tuning.
  • Mentor the engineers on the team and raise their engineering and AI practices.

What We're Looking For
  • 7–12 years of software engineering experience shipping production systems: backend, platform, or full stack.
  • Expert Python (10/10). You write idiomatic, production-quality code fluently on your own. You'll have AI coding assistants available, but you don't depend on them. You have built APIs and services in Python (FastAPI or comparable), you know its testing and packaging ecosystem, and you can write code others want to copy.
  • Very strong software fundamentals: data structures, API design, distributed systems, databases, concurrency, and security basics.
  • Full-stack ability preferred (React or comparable front end), but at minimum you can design and build APIs and backend systems end to end.
  • Good working knowledge of AWS (EKS or ECS, Lambda, IAM, networking) and Kubernetes, and some infrastructure-as-code (Terraform or CDK).

Headquartered in Miami, with offices in New York, London, Berlin, and Shenzhen, our 240+ team brings deep expertise across e-commerce, brand management, consumer retail, operational scaling, and M&A.

Since inception, we have acquired 30+ brands across Pet Care, Personal Care, Home Care, Supplements, Baby & Juvenile, Garden & Outdoor, Sports & Fitness, and Home & Lifestyle — completing 20+ acquisitions and delivering 16 consecutive quarters of like-for-like organic growth post-integration.

Our competitive advantage lies in a fully integrated operating system purpose-built to transform digital brands into omni-channel category leaders. Powered by a proprietary technology stack built on NetSuite ERP with 200+ data integrations, our platform enables brands to thrive across marketplaces, direct-to-consumer channels, and brick-and-mortar retail.

We focus on acquiring digital-first brands within carefully selected verticals, then applying tailored value creation playbooks that drive growth through innovation, expansion, and automation. We believe the next generation of consumer brands will be built differently — and we're building the AI-enabled retail tech platform to help them consolidate and win.

About the Role
You’ll lead organic social for one pet brand, Mighty Paw, across three channels: TikTok as the primary channel, Instagram as the secondary channel, and Facebook as the tertiary channel. Your job is to grow awareness, engagement, and community through content people want to watch, share, and come back for. The role has room to grow in scope and responsibility as the brand grows.

This role is approximately 80% content strategy and management and 20% hands-on content creation. You’ll own the content plan, manage creators and their output, and guide ideas from concept to published post. You’ll also film and edit select original content and work with our social commerce team
to adapt standout creator content for owned channels. For Mighty Paw, that means bringing the brand to life through products, practical tips, and everyday moments dog owners recognize.

What You’ll Do
Own Organic Social Strategy
- Build and manage weekly and monthly content calendars for Mighty Paw across TikTok, Instagram, and Facebook, prioritizing TikTok first, Instagram second, and Facebook third. Maintain a consistent brand voice and visual identity while tailoring content to each channel and leaving room for relevant

trends, sounds, and conversations.

  • Develop recurring series and platform-specific formats that give audiences a reason to follow and come back. Set creative priorities, brief creators, manage deadlines, and review content quality so the majority of your time stays focused on strategy and management.

    Manage Creators and Content Production
    - Manage the creators producing content for Mighty Paw as direct reports: set clear briefs and expectations, coordinate production schedules, give actionable feedback, and oversee delivery. Plan batched shoots and editing workflows to create a high volume of content efficiently.
    - Dedicate approximately 20% of your time to personally concepting, filming, and editing original product, lifestyle, educational, and trend-led content. Prioritize TikTok, adapt content for Instagram Reels and Facebook, and create supporting graphics and Stories as needed.
    - Partner with TikTok Shop affiliate and creator teams to identify strong videos and manage their adaptation for owned social channels. Guide hooks, captions, and calls to action that fit Mighty Paw and each platform, and oversee scheduling and publishing.
    - Work with Brand, Creative, and Social Commerce to support product launches, creator campaigns, and promotions. Partner with Marketing on creative concepts and variations for Meta ads.
Build an Engaged Community
- Oversee community management across TikTok, Instagram, and Facebook, ensuring timely responses to comments, messages, and mentions. Build relationships with followers and brand advocates, and route customer inquiries to the right teams.
- Invite participation through questions, polls, challenges, and features highlighting customers, creators, and their dogs. Explore tools such as Instagram broadcast channels.

Measure and Improve Performance- Track views, reach, engagement rate, comments, shares, saves, follower growth, and video retention across TikTok, Instagram, and Facebook using Sprout Social, Meta Business Manager, and native platform analytics. Prioritize insights and recommendations for TikTok, followed by Instagram and Facebook.
- Test hooks, editing styles, topics, and formats. Share weekly updates and monthly recommendations, and scale the approaches that deliver stronger results.
What You’ll Bring
-3–5 years of experience managing and growing organic social for consumer brands, with a strong focus on content strategy, editorial planning, and creator management.
-A portfolio of short-form video for TikTok or Instagram that shows your ability to shape content strategy, brief creators, and guide creative execution, alongside examples you have personally filmed, edited, or adapted from creator or user-generated content.
-Strong understanding of TikTok, Instagram, and Facebook culture and platform best practices, with particular depth in TikTok and the creative choices that influence retention and engagement.
-Experience managing online communities, maintaining a consistent brand voice across channels, and using performance data to improve creative. Experience batching content through planned shoots, coordinated production schedules, and repeatable editing workflows for efficient volume creation.
-Hands-on experience with Sprout Social, Meta Business Manager, TikTok native tools, and creative tools such as CapCut, Edits, Canva, Adobe Express, or Adobe Creative Suite.
-Strong written and verbal English communication, organization, and the ability to manage competing deadlines independently.

Experience managing a team or direct reports is a bonus, as this role will manage creators as direct reports. Having at least one dog is a plus, not a requirement. Experience in pet, DTC, or eCommerce is also a plus, as are photography, lighting, motion graphics, and advanced video editing skills.

What Success Looks Like
First 30 days
Learn Mighty Paw, audit TikTok, Instagram, and Facebook performance, review available creator content, and establish a channel-prioritized plan for content, publishing, creator management, and reporting.
First 60 days
Establish a consistent publishing cadence led by TikTok, with Instagram secondary and Facebook tertiary. Launch recurring series, set creator briefs and feedback routines, and build repeatable processes for batching production and repurposing affiliate content. Begin testing hooks and formats, introduce community initiatives, and develop paid social concepts with Marketing while maintaining the approximately 80% strategy and management / 20% hands-on creation balance.
Ongoing Grow
Mighty Paw’s organic reach, relevant followers, and meaningful interactions. Improve video retention and creative quality, scale effective formats across the three channels, and guide creative variations for Meta advertising. Evolve content volume, creator capacity, and the role’s scope as the brand grows.
Salary range: 80,000 - 90,000 USD

Build the Future
At McGraw Hill, we are dedicated to delivering digital learning experiences that transform education for learners and educators. Our focus is on creating seamless, impactful products that truly benefit our users while supporting growth and collaboration across teams. We foster a culture that values innovation, teamwork, and a balance between career growth and personal well-being.

How can you make an impact?

The Senior Technology Sourcing Analyst supports sourcing strategies and transactions across software, SaaS, cloud, hardware, AI, network, and technology services. The role provides advanced commercial analysis, leads defined sourcing activities, and develops recommendations that support negotiations, supplier decisions, and measurable value delivery.

Operating with greater autonomy than the Technology Sourcing Analyst, the Senior Analyst manages moderately complex sourcing events and renewals, analyzes supplier proposals and contract terms, and supports negotiations of technology agreements, including supplier-provided contracts, in partnership with sourcing leaders, Legal, and business stakeholders.

Success is demonstrated through accurate analysis, independent execution, proactive risk identification, clear stakeholder communication, and effective coaching of Analysts.

This is a remote position open to applicants authorized to work for any employer within the United States.

Category Strategy & Market Insight

  • Develop category and supplier insights using market trends, benchmarks, cost drivers, license or consumption data, and supplier performance information.
  • Translate analysis into recommendations that support category strategies, sourcing plans, renewals, and demand optimization.

Commercial & Negotiation Capability

  • Lead defined or moderately complex RFPs, renewals, supplier evaluations, and commercial workstreams; support sourcing leaders on larger or higher-risk transactions.
  • Develop pricing scenarios, cost and TCO models, negotiation materials, and supplier trade-off analyses across subscription, licensing, consumption, services, and hardware pricing models.
  • Review and support negotiation of technology agreements on supplier paper, including MSAs, SaaS and license agreements, order forms, SOWs, renewals, and amendments; identify pricing, scope, service-level, renewal, audit, termination, and transition risks for escalation.

Stakeholder & Influence Skills

  • Partner with Technology, Security, Privacy, Finance, Legal, and business stakeholders to clarify requirements, coordinate reviews, and maintain sourcing timelines.

Analytical & Financial Acumen

  • Build and validate advanced pricing, benchmarking, savings, cost-avoidance, TCO, and scenario analyses; ensure assumptions are accurate and traceable.
  • Maintain value tracking and sourcing reporting and identify opportunities related to license utilization, consumption, consolidation, and contract compliance.

Risk, Governance & Compliance

  • Maintain complete sourcing and contracting documentation in accordance with procurement governance and audit requirements.
  • Identify commercial, contractual, operational, and supplier risks and recommend practical mitigation actions.

Leadership & Talent Development

  • Coach Technology Sourcing Analysts, review analytical work, and improve templates, playbooks, and standardized sourcing processes.
  • Contribute to team capability building and share technology sourcing knowledge and market insights.

What You Bring:

  • Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree or professional certification preferred.
  • 5+ years of experience in strategic sourcing, technology procurement, category management, procurement analytics, finance, or a related commercial field.
  • Experience independently managing moderately complex sourcing events, renewals, or commercial workstreams.
  • Strong financial and analytical skills, including advanced pricing, benchmarking, savings, cost, TCO, and scenario analysis.
  • Experience evaluating supplier proposals and supporting negotiations for software, SaaS, cloud, hardware, AI, network, or technology services.
  • Working knowledge of technology contracts and commercial terms, including licensing and use rights, subscription and consumption models, SLAs, audit rights, renewals, termination, data and security obligations, and transition support.
  • Ability to identify risks and translate complex analysis into clear recommendations for sourcing leaders and stakeholders.
  • Strong organization, prioritization, communication, and stakeholder management skills; advanced proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint.
  • Demonstrated mentoring or informal leadership capability.
  • Experience reviewing or negotiating technology agreements presented on supplier paper, in collaboration with Legal.
  • Familiarity with sourcing platforms, contract lifecycle processes, supplier performance management, and technology risk reviews.
  • Professional certification such as CPSM or CIPS, or equivalent.

Why work for us?

The work you do at McGraw Hill will be work that matters. We are collectively building experiences that will help shape the future of education. Play your part and experience a sense of fulfilment that will inspire you to even greater heights.

jobs.description:
About the Role

At Cohypes, we grow and scale multiple brands in the health, beauty, and wellness space. We don't just build brands; we build operational systems that allow those brands to scale globally with speed and precision. As we continue to expand across the USA, UK, Europe, and Amazon marketplaces, we’re looking for a highly organized operations leader who is excited to take ownership of our global inventory and fulfillment ecosystem.

We believe great work happens when people feel valued. Here, your perspective matters, your ideas are welcome, and your voice has a real impact on how we grow. You’ll join a supportive team that encourages collaboration, open communication, and genuine trust.

About Us

We're looking for a Payments Optimization & Risk Manager to own the payments function across our e-commerce hub - a portfolio of DTC brands. You'll be the central owner of everything payments-related: acceptance rates, fraud and dispute management, PSP relationships, and payment platform health. This is a hands-on operational role split evenly between proactive optimization work (reporting, testing, PSP/account management) and reactive risk work (disputes, chargebacks, claims), with the goal of maximizing approval rates and minimizing loss from fraud and disputes across every brand.

You'll be the main point of contact for all things payments - internally for brand and ops teams, and externally with our payment providers.

Responsibilities

  • Own our payment platforms end-to-end: QA, reporting, documentation, and ongoing analysis
  • Act as the main point of contact for all payment-related questions across the business
  • Maintain up-to-date documentation on payment flows, configurations, and provider setups per brand
  • Own payment structure setup for new brands: PSP integration, business verification, and onboarding
  • Ensure new brands are fully configured and tested before launch
  • Evaluate and test new payment providers/PSPs, developing a strategy for when and how to bring them into the stack
  • Run structured analysis to compare provider performance (fees, approval rates, support quality)
  • Continuously track and test payment performance across all brands
  • Identify and act on opportunities to improve acceptance/authorization rates (e.g. routing, retry logic, checkout configuration)
  • Monitor fraud rates and tune fraud rules/filters to balance approval rates against fraud exposure
  • Own end-to-end response to disputes, claims, and chargebacks across all PSPs (Stripe, PayPal, etc.)
  • Compile evidence and submit representments within provider deadlines
  • Track dispute reason codes and translate patterns into recommendations for checkout, policy, or CS process changes
  • Monitor account health against PSP risk thresholds (e.g. dispute ratios, VAMP/SAFE-type programs) and flag risk early
  • Maintain daily, weekly, and monthly reporting on core payment KPIs
  • Present account health and performance trends to leadership and relevant sta

KPIs you’ll own:

  • Acceptance / authorization rate
  • Fraud rate
  • Processing fees (effective rate across providers)
  • PSP account health (standing, reserve/risk status, program thresholds)
  • Dispute / chargeback rate

Requirements

  • 2+ years of experience in a payments, risk, or fraud role, ideally within e-commerce or DTC
  • Hands-on experience managing payment service providers (e.g. Stripe, PayPal, or similar), including disputes and chargeback representment
  • Strong analytical skills — comfortable building and maintaining KPI trackers and pulling insights from payment/transaction data
  • Familiarity with fraud prevention tools, 3DS, and PSP risk programs (e.g. dispute ratio thresholds, monitoring programs)
  • Experience onboarding new merchant accounts/payment integrations
  • Excellent written communication for representment evidence, documentation, and cross-team collaboration
  • Comfortable owning a role independently, balancing reactive (disputes) and proactive (optimization) work day to day
  • Experience working across multiple brands or accounts simultaneously is a plus

Perks & Compensation

  • Compensation: 3,000-5,500 EUR gross per month, depending on experience
  • Fully remote
  • 40 hours/week
  • 20 days paid vacation annually
  • Paid bank holidays (Lithuanian bank holidays)
  • Opportunity to grow within a multi-brand e-commerce team in a fast-growing health & wellness portfolio

jobs.title: DOE Nuclear Conduct of Operations SME (4047)
jobs.description:
Navarro Research and Engineering is recruiting a DOE Nuclear Conduct of Operations SME (4047). This position is remote work as a consultant.

Navarro Research & Engineering is an award-winning federal contractor dedicated to partnering with clients to advance clean energy and deliver effective solutions for complex challenges in the nuclear and environmental fields. Joining Navarro means being a part of an exceptional team committed to quality and safety while also looking for innovative strategies to create value for the client’s success. Headquartered in Oak Ridge, Tennessee, Navarro has active programs in place across the nation for DOE/NNSA, NASA, and the Department of Defense.

Position Summary

Navarro is seeking an independent Conduct of Operations Subject Matter Expert (SME) to support the development and review of a Conduct of Operations Safety Management Program (SMP) description associated with an upcoming U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) Documented Safety Analysis (DSA). This remote consultant will supplement the project team by providing practical DOE nuclear operations expertise and producing defensible, DOE-quality documentation supporting the DSA and associated Technical Safety Requirements (TSRs).

Responsibilities

  • Develop, revise, and review the Conduct of Operations SMP description supporting a DOE DSA and associated TSRs.
  • Apply DOE O 422.1 requirements and applicable facility procedures, standards, and operational practices to SMP documentation.
  • Evaluate operating policies, procedure use and adherence, logkeeping, shift routines, communications, rounds, control of equipment status, and abnormal event response for completeness and consistency.
  • Assess how conduct of operations controls support implementation of safety limits, limiting conditions for operation, surveillance requirements, and administrative controls.
  • Identify technical gaps, inconsistencies, and compliance concerns and recommend practical, defensible resolutions.
  • Coordinate with safety basis personnel, operations managers, shift personnel, training staff, facility representatives, and program owners to ensure the SMP description accurately reflects implementation.
  • Produce clear, traceable, and technically defensible documentation suitable for DOE and contractor review.
  • Support comment resolution, document revisions, technical reviews, and related DSA deliverables.

Requirements

  • Demonstrated DOE or NNSA nuclear facility operations experience with direct responsibility for conduct of operations implementation or assessment.
  • Experience developing, implementing, assessing, or reviewing a Conduct of Operations SMP supporting DSAs and TSRs.
  • Working knowledge of 10 CFR 830, DOE O 422.1, DOE-STD-3009, and DOE nuclear facility conduct of operations expectations.
  • Prior experience preparing, reviewing, or supporting conduct of operations sections of DSA, SMP, safety basis, or related nuclear facility documentation.
  • Ability to independently review complex technical material and produce clear, accurate, and defensible DOE-quality documentation.
  • Strong written communication, technical judgment, and collaboration skills.
  • Ability to perform work remotely as an independent consultant.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior experience as an operations manager, shift manager, facility manager, senior operator, operations assurance lead, or DOE operational oversight professional.
  • Previous experience supporting DOE Idaho programs, facilities, management and operating contractors, or DOE-ID oversight activities.
  • Experience participating in DOE operational readiness reviews, readiness assessments, surveillances, audits, or conduct of operations assessments.
  • Background as a retired or recently separated DOE, NNSA, national laboratory, or management and operating contractor operations professional.
  • Availability to support intermittent assignments as project needs develop over the next several months.

Education and Experience

  • Education and experience requirements will depend on the candidate’s operations background. Candidates must possess sufficient technical education, operational training, qualification history, and directly relevant DOE nuclear facility experience to serve as a credible subject matter expert and independently perform the required document development and review work.

Due to the nature of the government contract requirements and/or clearances requirements, US citizenship is required.

Navarro is an equal-opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, race, religion, color, national origin, age, disability, veteran’s status, or any classification protected by applicable state or local law..

jobs.title: Lead Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Overview

Build the Future

At McGraw Hill, we are dedicated to delivering digital learning experiences that transform education for learners and educators. Our focus is on creating seamless, impactful products that truly benefit our users while supporting growth and collaboration across teams. We foster a culture that values innovation, teamwork, and a balance between career growth and personal well-being.

How can you make an impact?

We’re looking for a Lead Engineer who enjoys solving difficult problems and helping a team do its best work. You’ll stay hands-on, help engineers make thoughtful decisions, and work closely with product and design partners to deliver software that helps students learn and educators teach.

You’ll also help shape how we build. We expect our leads to question assumptions, bring ideas backed by evidence, and take responsibility for turning those ideas into improvements. That includes making agentic development an effective part of the team’s everyday work.

This is a remote position open to applicants authorized to work for any employer within the United States.

Your Role On The Team

You’ll provide technical leadership for your team, guiding decisions and helping engineers move work from an initial problem through delivery and production support. You’ll balance immediate customer needs with the longer-term health of the software, choosing solutions that fit the problem and making trade-offs clear.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role with no direct reports. You’ll partner with an Engineering Manager who owns people management, staffing, and performance. Your leadership comes through your judgment, contributions, and ability to earn trust.

We value leads who help others grow in confidence and independence. You should be comfortable making a decision, inviting disagreement, and changing your mind when the evidence warrants it.

What You'll Do

  • Deliver customer value incrementally. Work with product and design to understand the problem, clarify outcomes, and break work into useful, achievable releases.
  • Contribute product ideas. Bring a perspective from the intersection of product and technology to proactively propose new product enhancements and capabilities.
  • Guide technical decisions. Help the team evaluate options, resolve uncertainty, and coordinate dependencies. Give engineers room to own decisions within a shared direction.
  • Build alongside the team. Contribute frontend interfaces, backend application code, and APIs. Use implementation, prototyping, debugging, and review to move difficult work forward.
  • Improve how we develop with agents. Use coding agents for investigation, planning, implementation, testing, and review. Help the team provide useful context, structure work, and verify results.Engineers remain accountable for the software they deliver.
  • Build quality into delivery. Work with relevant partners, including SRE, security, and UX, to address reliability, accessibility, and safe releases. Follow through on how changes behave in production.
  • Develop other engineers. Mentor through pairing, design discussions, and constructive feedback. Share context and help teammates solve problems independently.
  • Drive practical improvements. Identify recurring friction in the codebase or development process, propose changes, and assess whether they improve delivery and quality.

What You Bring:

  • Experience providing hands-on technical leadership and helping a team deliver complex software.
  • Experience building modern web applications across frontend and backend, with depth in at least one area and the ability to work across both.
  • Sound judgment about design, testing, and maintainability. You can explain trade-offs and recognize when to involve a specialist.
  • A product mindset: you seek to understand customer needs and use that understanding to guide engineering decisions.
  • Practical experience with agentic development.
  • A collaborative leadership style. You listen, make decisions, give useful feedback, and support others without relying on management authority.
  • Clear communication with engineering colleagues and partners in other disciplines.

Technology Environment:

  • Back-end: Java (most common), Go
  • Front-end:TypeScript, React.js, NextJS, Angular, NgRx/RxJS, and Playwright
  • Databases: Relational, NoSQL, and Graph
  • CI/CD, Infrastructure: GitHub, SonarQube, Docker, Kubernetes, Datadog, New Relic
  • Amazon Web Services (AWS): EKS, ECS, RDS, Lambda, and others
  • Harnesses: Claude and GitHub Copilot

Why work for us?

AI is changing how people learn and how educators support them. McGraw Hill has the educational content, subject expertise, and relationships with educators to help lead that change. The opportunity is to bring those strengths together with AI to build learning experiences that help students understand more and give educators more time to teach.

As a Lead Engineer, you’ll help turn that opportunity into working software. You’ll influence what we build and how we build it, including how we use agents in our own engineering work.

If you’re excited by the chance to shape AI’s role in education and help a team turn ambitious ideas into useful products, we’d like to hear from you.

The pay range for this position is between $145,000 - $180,000 annually, however, base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and location. An annual bonus plan may be provided as part of the compensation package, in addition to a full range of medical and/or other benefits, depending on the position offered. Additionally, McGraw Hill recruiters and authorized representatives will never request sensitive information in email.

Validation sets up the provider side of every records request before retrieval starts.   • Passionate about making advanced fission a reality

jobs.title: Customer Success Manager
jobs.description:
About the Role

BusRight builds routing and transportation software that helps school districts get students to school and home safely. As a Customer Success Manager, you’ll own a book of districts and be responsible for one thing above all: making sure every one of them gets real, measurable results from BusRight and wants to keep working with us year after year.

You’ll be the person each district trusts most at BusRight. You’ll learn their goals, build a success plan with them, track progress against it, and show them the return they’re getting. When a district starts to struggle, you’ll see it early and do something about it. Our Support team owns tickets and our Implementation team owns onboarding and setup, so your time goes where it matters most, with your customers.

What You’ll Do

  • Build and own a success plan for every district in your book. Sit down with district leaders, understand what they’re trying to accomplish, set goals together, and review progress and ROI with them on a regular cadence.
  • Drive adoption across the platform. Know which parts of BusRight each district is using and which they aren’t, close training gaps (especially after staff turnover), and help them get more out of the product every year.
  • Own retention for your book. Every district renews every year, so you’ll lead the value conversation first and the renewal conversation after, starting four to six months ahead of the renewal date.
  • Spot risk early and act on it. Watch health, usage and sentiment, flag at-risk accounts, and build and run recovery plans that get them back to healthy.
  • Build relationships at every level of the district. You’ll join the implementation kickoff for new districts and get to know superintendents, business officials and transportation directors from day one, then keep those relationships strong with consistent, scheduled engagement.
  • Find growth opportunities. When a district’s needs grow, you’ll spot it and partner with our Sales team to bring the right solution forward.
  • Be the voice of the customer inside BusRight. Share what you’re hearing with Product, Support and Implementation so we keep getting better for districts.

What You’ll Bring

  • 3 to 5 years of experience as a Customer Success Manager at a SaaS company, managing your own book of business
  • EdTech or K-12 experience is a big plus. If you’ve worked with school districts before, you already know how they make decisions, how budgets work and what the school year feels like, and that matters here.
  • A track record of retaining customers and driving adoption, with results you can walk us through
  • Experience building success plans and leading business reviews or ROI conversations with executive stakeholders
  • Strong organization and a habit of using data to decide where to spend your time
  • Comfort working in Salesforce and a customer success platform
  • Steadiness under pressure. Back to school (July through September) is our busiest season, and districts count on us to show up.
  • Ability to travel up to 15% of the time

Who Thrives Here

  • You believe in Magical Hospitality, one of the values our team holds closest. For us, being responsive and kind is only the starting point. You anticipate what a district needs
  • before they ask, follow through on the little things, and make every person you work with feel like they’re your only customer.
  • You take ownership of your accounts and don’t wait for someone else to fix a problem.
  • You’re proactive. You’d rather pick up the phone and call a district than wait for them to call you.
  • You lead with curiosity, ask good questions and bring a point of view.
  • You like building things. We’re growing quickly and putting new processes in place, and you’ll help shape how Customer Success works here.
  • You see feedback as a gift and keep getting better.

Why BusRight

  • Your work directly affects whether students get to school safely and on time.
  • You’ll join a Customer Success team that’s growing and investing in how we work, from success plans to new playbooks and tools.
  • Remote work with a culture built on trust and collaboration
  • Competitive compensation, equity and benefits
