jobs.title: Group Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Catalyst Capital is a profitable, bootstrapped holding company building a diversified financial services group - education, publishing, software, wealth and tax planning tools, investment products and proprietary trading technology - funded entirely from its own operating cash. We have never taken outside capital.

The cash engine is Decentralized Masters, a DeFi education business that went from zero to 150+ people, 4,500+ paying members and roughly $48.6M of FY26 revenue at ~25% earnings before tax in four years. That engine funds everything else on this page.

In build over the next 18 months

  • A lifestyle community membership - consumer membership economics, distinct from education.
  • A business mastermind on the Hampton model - high-net-worth peer community, recurring and relationship-led.
  • A regulated investment fund. The capstone. AUM reporting, investor relations, NAV calculation, fund administration, audit and regulatory infrastructure. At most companies this alone is a full-time CFO mandate.

Why This Role Exists

A single education business at this revenue and margin commands a private-market multiple in the mid single digits of earnings. A diversified group - education, publishing, software, wealth and tax planning tools, investment products and a regulated fund, each valued on its own sector methodology and connected by real shared-services and synergy architecture - is a fundamentally different asset.

Closing that gap is the job. Concretely, you will:

  • Build the sum-of-the-parts valuation framework across every business unit, with a defensible methodology and comparables set for each.
  • Structure each entity so that it maximises its own multiple, and structure the group so the whole is worth more than the parts.
  • Take the group from founder-run reporting to institutional-grade financials that survive a quality-of-earnings review and a full due diligence process.
  • Take the group to market early - deliberately ahead of a formal process - and convert what buyers and advisers tell us into operational change while there is still time to act on it.
  • Build the group equity story and the materials that put it in front of institutional buyers, and run the process alongside the CEO and advisers.
  • Design the employee incentive architecture at group level, so the people who carry each unit are aligned before a transaction rather than after it.
  • Stand up the regulated fund and the investor infrastructure behind it.
  • Protect and improve the economics of the cash engine while all of the above happens. If DM slows, none of the rest matters.

How This Role Is Resourced

You are not being hired to close the books. A Finance Manager reports to you and owns day-to-day financial operations - the monthly close, the accounting system, payroll, reconciliations, deferred revenue schedules and the chart of accounts. Beneath them sit a Financial Controller and an Accounting & Payroll Specialist.

What You Will Own

1. Enterprise Value & Capital Events (Primary)

  • Own the sum-of-the-parts valuation model: the methodology, comparables and defensible assumptions for each business unit, and the roll-up into a coherent group valuation.
  • Identify and drive the highest-value levers to increase group enterprise value - margin, retention, revenue quality, recurring mix, entity structure, and the synergy story between units.
  • Take the group to institutional readiness: three years of clean, comparable financials per entity, a quality-of-earnings-survivable position, a populated data room and a diligence-ready control environment.
  • Build the group equity story, the information memorandum and the management presentation, and be credible in the room with institutional buyers and their advisers.
  • Run the capital event process alongside the CEO and external advisers - buyer engagement, diligence management, negotiation support, and the post-transaction reporting obligations that follow.

2. Holdco Architecture, Systems & Synergy

  • Design the holding-company structure: which entities sit where, in which jurisdictions, and why - with counsel and tax advisers.
  • Select and implement the group ERP and consolidation platform. Own the selection criteria, the sequence and the delivery.
  • Build shared services where they create real margin and demonstrable synergy value, and resist them where they destroy unit-level clarity.
  • Set intercompany and transfer pricing policy across a group where one entity generates leads, another converts them, a third delivers the product and a fourth manages money - across the UAE, the US and potentially Europe.
  • Produce unit-level P&Ls that roll up cleanly and let leadership see which businesses earn their capital.

3. Capital Allocation Across Unlike Businesses

  • Own the framework that decides where the next dollar of operating cash goes - paid media, headcount, software build, fund seed capital, acquisitions or reserve - with an explicit hurdle rate and time horizon for each.
  • Allocate across assets with genuinely different return profiles, risk characteristics and payback periods, and defend the trade-offs to the CEO with a model behind them.
  • Own group headcount and cost strategy. Be the person who can say no, with numbers.

4. The Cash Engine - Direct-Response Economics

Required, not optional. The group is funded by performance marketing and will be for the foreseeable future.

  • Own CAC, LTV, LTV:CAC, ROAS, CPQC, contribution margin and cash payback by funnel, offer, channel and cohort.
  • Own the front-end versus back-end monetisation model, and the timing mismatch between media spend today and payment-plan collections over twelve months.
  • Improve pricing and offer-ladder economics across low, mid and high ticket.
  • Model cohort behaviour, renewals, churn, refunds, chargebacks and payment-plan default — and build them into the forecast rather than discovering them later.
  • Set the media spend guardrails that keep the group liquid in a bad month without capping a good one.

5. Fund Structuring, Regulation & Investor Infrastructure

  • Lead jurisdiction and structure selection for the investment fund with counsel - DIFC, ADGM or otherwise - and own the trade-offs.
  • Stand up the operating infrastructure: fund administration, NAV calculation, audit, fee and carry mechanics, subscription and redemption processes.
  • Build investor reporting infrastructure capable of serving hundreds of investors on a reliable cadence.
  • Own regulatory compliance across the group: UAE regimes including VARA and ADGM where applicable, FTC and advertising-claims compliance in marketing, securities considerations across the investment products, and the regulatory perimeter around the wealth and tax planning tools.

6. Treasury, Cash & Group Risk

  • Own rolling 13-week and 12-month cash forecasts at entity and group level, and the liquidity view across the whole structure.
  • Optimise working capital - processor reserves and holdbacks, refund provisions, receivable ageing on payment plans.
  • Own banking, merchant accounts and payment processors: redundancy, concentration risk, chargeback ratios and cost of processing.
  • Set treasury policy for digital asset exposure: custody, counterparty limits, stablecoin policy, valuation and controls.

7. Legal & Corporate Affairs

You are not expected to be a lawyer. You are expected to own the function so the CEO does not have to.

  • Own the relationship with, and the budget for, external counsel, auditors, tax advisers and transaction advisers across jurisdictions.
  • Own the corporate calendar across every entity - filings, licences, renewals, tax deadlines. Nothing lapses, particularly not during diligence.
  • Own commercial terms on major partnerships, vendor, affiliate and talent agreements; legal drafting stays with counsel.

Requirements

What You Must Bring

Required

  • 10-20 years in finance, including 3+ years as CFO, Group CFO or VP Finance with full P&L and balance sheet accountability.
  • Direct, hands-on experience of a transaction. You have been on a sell-side or minority sale process and can describe what you personally built - the model, the CIM, the data room, the diligence responses - and what went wrong.
  • Multi-entity holdco or portfolio experience. You have run finance across several unlike businesses, not one company with divisions, and you can explain how you consolidated and how you allocated between them.
  • Sum-of-the-parts fluency. You can value a software business, a subscription publishing business, a services business and a fee-earning investment business, and explain why each methodology is the right one.
  • Performance-marketing economics. You have owned unit economics in a business spending meaningful money on paid acquisition - CAC, LTV, payback, front end versus back end. Required. Not the defining filter, but a candidate who cannot do this cannot protect our cash engine.
  • Multi-jurisdiction experience with real consolidation, ideally including the UAE, the US and Europe.
  • Experience owning the relationship with external counsel, auditors and transaction advisers.
  • Fully conversant in both IFRS and US GAAP, and able to defend technical positions under scrutiny.
  • A prolific, demonstrable user of AI tools in finance work - you can show us what you have built or automated.

Strongly Preferred

  • Financial services depth - you have worked across at least two of publishing, education, software, wealth management or fund management.
  • You have structured or operated an investment fund: jurisdiction, administration, NAV, fee and carry mechanics, investor reporting.
  • PE-backed or PE operating experience - you understand how institutional buyers think and what they discount.
  • Crypto and digital asset exposure. You do not need to be a trader, but you cannot be squeamish about the asset class.
  • Subscription accounting and deferred revenue depth across high-ticket, payment plan and recurring products.

Do Not Apply If…

  • Your entire career has been in large corporate environments with no exposure to founder-led, high-growth or PE-backed businesses.
  • You have never been close to a transaction and would be learning the process on our timeline.
  • You have never treated paid acquisition as a strategic cost lever.
  • You need six months to ramp before you add value.
  • You prefer slow-moving, consensus-heavy environments, or you fold when a founder pushes back.
  • You do not want legal, regulatory and corporate affairs coordination in your remit.
  • You want to build a large team before you have personally fixed the numbers.
  • You are not actively using AI tools in your work today.

Personality & Cultural Fit

  • Direct communicator who challenges the founders with data, in the room, in real time.
  • Equally credible with a PE partner and with a media buyer. Both conversations happen in the same week here.
  • Entrepreneurial and comfortable in ambiguity - you build the answer rather than wait for the brief.
  • Zero tolerance for sloppy reporting, in your team or in yourself.
  • Builder mentality. Comfortable in the model and in the detail when it matters.

Benefits

What We Offer

  • Competitive base, depending on transaction and holdco experience.
  • Performance bonus tied to enterprise value creation, not just operating margin.
  • A transaction bonus on a successful capital event - the upside here is material and it is the point of the role.
  • Equity participation under the C-suite framework, structured so you have skin in the game before the event rather than after it.
  • UAE-based roles are tax-free, which materially changes take-home pay.
  • Direct access to the founders, a peer relationship with the Group COO, and genuine authority over how capital is deployed.
  • An inherited finance team, so you are building the architecture rather than clearing a backlog alone.

If you are a divisional CFO looking for a bigger version of the job you already have, this is not it.

If you have built the financial architecture that made a diversified group worth substantially more than the sum of its operating profits - and you want to do it again, from profitability, with your own mandate - we should talk.

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced, sharp, and independent Home Health Prior Authorization & Eligibility Specialist to join our authorization team.

Our agency operates with a heavily managed-care census (~80% HMO/IPA), and accuracy at the front end of every referral is critical. You will take ownership of reviewing incoming Start-of-Care (SOC) referrals, verifying active eligibility, identifying the exact responsible payer, and securing initial authorizations and reauthorizations for Skilled Nursing (SN) and Physical Therapy (PT) visits.

This is not a training role, a patient-scheduling role, or a medical billing role. You will focus exclusively on payer communication, eligibility verification, and authorization approvals—ensuring zero missed checks, zero lost admissions, and clean downstream claim processing. While we will train you on our internal protocols and Synergy EMR workflows, you must bring deep, day-one mastery of home health authorization fundamentals.

Requirements

Key Responsibilities

1. Start-of-Care (SOC) Eligibility & Responsible Payer Verification

  • Promptly review incoming Start-of-Care referrals received through referral portals and immediately initiate eligibility verification so zero admissions are missed or delayed.
  • Go beyond portal checks: Call insurance carriers and IPAs directly to confirm active coverage, home health benefit carve-outs, and exact payer responsibility to prevent downstream claim rejections.
  • Identify discrepancies between portal listings and live payer records, asking targeted follow-up questions rather than accepting unclear or conflicting representative answers at face value.

2. Initial Authorizations & Reauthorizations (SN & PT)

  • Manage an independent daily caseload of 7–15 authorization cases (up to 20 during peak periods).
  • Process initial home health authorizations and submit timely reauthorizations for ongoing Skilled Nursing (SN) and Physical Therapy (PT) visits.
  • Gather and submit clinical documentation (OASIS summaries, therapy evaluations, physician orders) required to meet payer medical necessity guidelines.

3. HMO, IPA & Network Navigation

  • Navigate complex HMO plans, Independent Physician Associations (IPAs), and delegated medical groups (including Blue Cross Blue Shield, Health Net, UnitedHealthcare, Providence, Optum, Regal, and Lakeside).
  • Document all payer call reference numbers, representative names, authorization numbers, approved visit counts, and effective dates inside Synergy EMR.

Must-Have Qualifications (Day-One Non-Negotiables)

  • Direct Home Health Agency Experience (Mandatory): Proven, hands-on background working specifically inside the authorization department of a Home Health Care Agency. (General outpatient clinic or hospital referral experience alone is not sufficient).
  • Independent Authorization Mastery: Complete command of Start-of-Care eligibility checks, responsible payer identification, and SN/PT reauthorizations without needing foundational training.
  • HMO & IPA Expertise: Strong working knowledge of managed care networks, HMO carve-outs, and California IPAs (e.g., Optum, Regal, Lakeside, Health Net, Blue Cross Blue Shield, United, Providence).
  • Investigative Phone Skills: High confidence calling insurance carriers via RingCentral, spotting conflicting payer information, and escalating or probing until accurate answers are confirmed.
  • Systems: Familiarity with Synergy EMR is a strong plus; high proficiency navigating multi-payer portals (Availity, NaviNet, etc.) is required.

Our client is a California-based digital marketing agency specializing in lead generation for outdoor living contractors, including patio cover, deck, and screen enclosure businesses. The agency helps contractors generate opportunities through digital marketing and improve the way they manage and convert incoming leads.

The Opportunity

We’re looking for a proactive, marketing-savvy Client Success Manager to independently own client relationships, retention, communication, and account success.

You’ll manage approximately 30 accounts initially, growing toward 37–40, and coordinate with a fulfillment team of approximately four to five people. Reporting directly to agency leadership, you’ll make sure clients receive consistent support, actionable guidance, and reliable delivery.

This is a client success role that calls for strong marketing literacy. Dedicated media buyers handle campaign execution, while you own the client relationship and the outcomes around it.

What You’ll Do

  • Own client onboarding, pre-launch meetings, and recurring weekly, biweekly, or monthly check-ins based on each account’s needs.
  • Build trusted relationships with U.S.-based contractor business owners and serve as their primary point of contact.
  • Monitor account health, identify churn risks early, resolve escalations, and proactively communicate next steps.
  • Review Meta Ads and lead-generation performance, explain campaign reports, and translate findings into actionable recommendations.
  • Coach clients on lead response, follow-up, CRM usage, and conversion opportunities, and distinguish campaign issues from downstream sales and lead-management problems.

  • Provide leadership with regular updates on client satisfaction, performance, risks, and operational priorities.
  • Identify appropriate upsell opportunities and proactively generate client reviews, testimonials, and referrals.

How Success Is Measured

  • Client retention of approximately 95%.
  • At least five new client reviews per month.
  • Approximately two to three video testimonials or interviews per month.
  • Approximately two successful upsells per month.
  • Consistent, proactive client communication, timely issue resolution, and reliable follow-through.
  • Clear visibility over account performance, client requests, and team deliverables without routine founder oversight.

Your First 90 Days

  • Days 1–30: Learn the agency’s services, client portfolio, campaign reporting, systems, and team workflows, and begin taking ownership of client communication and assigned accounts.
  • Days 31–60: Independently manage an increasing share of the portfolio, establish recurring account reviews, and identify retention and lead-conversion opportunities.
  • Days 61–90: Own the assigned portfolio and coordinate delivery with minimal supervision, proactively addressing client risks and tracking agreed KPIs.

These milestones describe the intended ramp-up approach.

Compensation

  • Base: CAD $56,000 annually.
  • Variable: Performance-based bonuses.
  • Target OTE: CAD $70,000–$78,000 annually, including performance-based bonuses. Bonus earnings depend on performance and are not guaranteed.

Requirements

What We’re Looking For

  • Approximately 3–5 years of relevant experience in Client Success, Account Management, or a closely related client-facing marketing role.
  • Strong understanding of Meta Ads, lead generation, campaign reporting, and conversion metrics.
  • Demonstrated experience managing multiple client accounts, handling challenging conversations, and supporting client retention.
  • Excellent spoken and written English, with the confidence and interpersonal skills to advise U.S.-based business owners.
  • Working knowledge of CRM systems and lead-management workflows, plus the ability to learn GoHighLevel quickly if you’re not already familiar with it.
  • Experience coordinating internal teams, tracking deliverables, and taking ownership of follow-through.
  • Strong organizational skills, reliability, attention to detail, initiative, and the ability to work independently during required hours.
  • Based in Canada or South Africa.
  • Availability to work 9 AM–6 PM, with a one-hour break.

Nice to Have

  • Previous experience in a digital marketing or lead-generation agency.
  • Experience supporting outdoor living, home services, construction, or contractor businesses.
  • Experience managing high-volume client portfolios and coaching business owners on lead conversion.
  • Previous team leadership or operational coordination experience.
  • Familiarity with GoHighLevel, Slack, ClickUp, Zapier, and CRM integrations or automations.
  • Demonstrated success with retention, upselling, testimonials, reviews, and client recovery.

Benefits

  • Competitive base compensation: CAD $56,000 annually.
  • Performance-based bonuses: Target OTE of CAD $70,000–$78,000 annually.
  • Paid time off: 10 paid days off and five paid sick days.
  • U.S. holidays off.
  • 100% remote work from Canada or South Africa.
  • Ownership and impact: Independently own a client portfolio and directly influence client retention and results.
  • Growth potential: As the agency grows, the role may expand in team coordination and client ownership.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Company Summary

Started in 2023, HeyMax is one of the fastest growing fintech companies in Singapore. We leverage technology to revolutionize the way people maximize their miles and rewards through merchant affiliation, credit card rewards, and more. We are committed to simplifying personal finance and delivering equitable personal finance optimizations to our customers. For businesses, HeyMax is shaping up to be the most advanced customer acquisition platform for high-value customers.

HeyMax was started by 4 ex-Meta veteran engineers, joined by a founding team of talented builders and operators from Endowus, Aspire, Funding Societies, SingSaver, and beyond. HeyMax is supported by a list of top-tier investors that includes founders, VCs, and industry leaders.

What We're Looking For

Ever found yourself trapped in endless meetings where discussions spiral, approvals pile up, and not a single line of meaningful code gets shipped? Or spent your time optimizing a tiny corner of a massive system, wondering whether your work actually matters?

If those scenarios sound familiar, HeyMax is built for a different kind of engineer. We are a fast-moving fintech startup where your work matters, your ideas count, and you can make a direct difference for users.

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer who wants to build meaningful products in an environment where engineering impact is direct, visible, and amplified by AI. You should be the kind of engineer who already uses tools like Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, or similar systems to move faster across implementation, debugging, testing, and code review.

You care about shipping quickly, but not carelessly. You bring strong judgment, technical depth, and the ability to turn ambiguous product ideas into reliable systems used by real customers across multiple markets.

What You'll Do

  • Build High-Impact Product Features: Design, implement, and ship features that improve how users earn, track, and redeem rewards through HeyMax.
  • Use AI-Augmented Development: Apply AI tools across your daily workflow, from exploring requirements and generating implementation plans to testing, debugging, and reviewing code.
  • Own Technical Design: Make sound design decisions for the systems and features you work on, balancing speed, reliability, maintainability, and product impact.
  • Stay Hands-On: Spend most of your time building. We value senior engineers who stay close to the code and understand the details of what they ship.
  • Improve Engineering Quality: Write clean, maintainable code, improve observability, strengthen tests, and help keep our systems reliable as we scale.
  • Collaborate Across Functions: Work closely with product, design, business, and operations teams to translate customer and business needs into practical technical solutions.
  • Mentor Through Example: Support other engineers through code reviews, pairing, thoughtful feedback, and by sharing effective AI-assisted development patterns.

Responsibilities

With great power comes great responsibility. Here's what you'll own:

  • Build and maintain production-grade systems across mobile, backend, infrastructure, data, or AI-related surfaces.
  • Take projects from ambiguous requirements to shipped, measurable outcomes.
  • Contribute to architecture discussions and own technical decisions within your project areas.
  • Use AI tools thoughtfully to accelerate development while maintaining strong engineering judgment.
  • Review code, improve implementation quality, and help the team move quickly without sacrificing reliability.
  • Partner with cross-functional teams to understand business context and deliver practical solutions.
  • Identify technical debt, reliability gaps, and opportunities to improve developer velocity.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Strong software engineering experience, ideally with a track record of delivering complex projects end-to-end.
  • Technical depth in one or more areas: mobile, backend, infrastructure, data, or AI.
  • Experience building and operating production systems used by real customers.
  • Strong product sense and ability to make pragmatic tradeoffs under ambiguity.
  • Active use of AI coding tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, or similar systems.
  • Strong communication skills and ability to collaborate with both technical and non-technical teammates.
  • High ownership mindset: you care about outcomes, not just tickets.
  • Bonus: experience with fintech, loyalty/rewards systems, or multi-region deployments across Southeast Asia.

Our Mission

At HeyMax, we believe that travel brings joy and fosters empathy. Our mission is to make aspirational travel experiences accessible to everyone.

Our Vision

We have created a platform that connects you to the brands you love. Every time you interact, your purchases are rewarded in the form of a universal travel currency, Max Miles, to travel anywhere.

Our Values

  • Deliver Long-Term Customer Value: Every decision starts with our users. We listen, design, and iterate with their needs at the center.
  • Transparency: Trust is built on honesty. Whether it is our product, policies, or partnerships, we communicate openly and proactively so our team and users can rely on us to deliver exactly what we promise.
  • Be The Owner: Ownership is our mantra. More than just accountability, it is taking initiative, making informed decisions, and leading with integrity. We each own the impact we have on our customers, the well-being of our team, and the outcomes of our actions.

jobs.title: Head of Engineering
jobs.description:
At Magentus, our goal is to create a healthier society through technology. We do that by delivering smart workflows that connect people, systems, and data - making care more intelligent, efficient, and accessible. Whether it’s supporting clinicians, streamlining operations, or improving patient outcomes, we’re here to make a real difference in healthcare through digital innovation.

As part of the Magentus Group, Labflow, is helping pathology providers deliver critical healthcare services through reliable, secure, cloud-hosted technology.

We provide laboratory information systems, integrations and reporting solutions that support healthcare organisations across Australia. Our platforms sit at the intersection of healthcare, cloud infrastructure and software, helping laboratories operate efficiently while delivering better outcomes for patients.

About the Role

You will lead engineering at Labflow: the team, the delivery, the quality of what ships, and the technical direction that supports it. You report to the CEO and sit on the leadership team.

You and the Head of Product are jointly accountable for delivery. Product owns what we build and why. You own how it gets built, when it lands, and whether it holds up in production. The two of you agree the roadmap, make the tradeoffs together, and give the rest of the company one answer on what is shipping and when.

This is a hands-on leadership role in a small team. You will not write most of the code, but you will read it, review designs, and be able to step into an incident or a hard technical decision with credibility.

The role is fully remote, and so is the team. Much of the work happens in writing and across time zones.

What you will own:

Delivery

  • Plan and run delivery with the Head of Product: scope, sequencing, estimates and dates the company can trust.

  • Surface risk early. When a date will slip, say so while there is still time to change scope.

  • Keep work flowing: clear tickets, small changes, short review cycles, few things in progress at once.

Team

  • Lead, coach and grow the engineers. Regular one-to-ones, honest feedback, clear expectations.

  • Hire: define the roles, run the process, close the candidates, onboard them well.

  • Deal with underperformance promptly and fairly.

  • Build a team that does not depend on any one person, including you.

Technical direction and quality

  • Own architecture decisions and the record of why they were made.

  • Set and hold the engineering bar: code review, testing, release practice, incident response.

  • Balance new work against technical debt, and make that tradeoff visible to Product.

  • Own production reliability: monitoring, on-call, post-incident review, follow-through.

Safety, security and compliance

  • Own engineering's part in clinical safety: changes that touch patient-affecting paths get the scrutiny they need before they ship.

  • Own secure development practice and engineering's controls under ISO 27001.

AI-assisted engineering

  • We build heavily with AI coding agents. You will own how the team uses them: the workflows, the guardrails, the review standards, and where a human must stay in the loop.

Operating the function

  • Engineering budget, tooling and vendors.

  • Represent engineering to the leadership team, and to customers and auditors when needed.

  • Report honestly on progress, risk and team health.

What we are looking for:

Must have

  • Led an engineering team as the accountable manager, including hiring and performance management.

  • A track record of shipping reliable software on dates you committed to, in partnership with a product leader.

  • Strong technical background as a senior engineer or architect. You can review a design, read a pull request, and tell a sound decision from a fragile one.

  • Experience running production systems where downtime or bad data has real consequences.

  • Clear, direct communication, written and spoken, with engineers and non-engineers alike.

  • Experience leading a remote or distributed team.

  • Comfort in a small company: little process to inherit, a lot to decide, and no layer below you to delegate ambiguity to.

Strongly preferred

  • Experience in healthcare, diagnostics, laboratory systems or another regulated domain.

  • Worked under ISO 27001, SOC 2 or a comparable security framework.

  • Practical experience running a team that uses AI coding agents day to day.

Nice to have

  • Healthcare interoperability standards (HL7 v2, FHIR, LOINC, SNOMED CT).

  • Experience with our stack: Rails/AWS.

Join Today!

At Magentus, we live our values every day:

  • One Team – We collaborate and support each other

  • Constant Evolution – We embrace change and keep improving

  • We Care – About our people, our customers, and our impact

  • Make A Difference – We’re here to create real, positive change

  • Trust – We do what we say and act with integrity

What’s in it for you:

  • Flexible work options to support work-life balance

  • Learning and development programs to grow your career

  • A supportive, inclusive team culture

  • Opportunities to work across departments and expand your skills

  • A purpose-driven company where your work truly matters

Ready to bring your energy and organisation to a team that cares? Apply now and help us make a difference at Magentus!

jobs.title: Recruiter (BBS974)
jobs.description:
We're looking for a Recruiter to run screening and hiring operations for an early-stage GovTech startup building a modern planning and permitting platform for local governments. You will screen candidates, keep the applicant tracking system clean, schedule interviews, coordinate team days, and help the founders and hiring managers move great people through the process quickly.

This is a hands-on seat inside a small, fast-moving team. You will recruit across product management, design, and go-to-market roles, so you need to understand what a strong candidate looks like in each. A lot of the job is the work that makes a hiring process feel good for candidates and easy for the team: sharp screens, fast scheduling, clear notes, and an ATS that tells the truth. The team hires for strengths and potential, so you will need good judgment, not just keywords. If you have recruited at an early-stage startup, are comfortable running a lean process, and take pride in a candidate experience that reflects well on the company, this role is a strong fit.

Why You'll Want to Join

  • You will be paid in USD (bi-monthly: every 15th and 30th)
  • Paid Time Off in accordance with company policy
  • Observance of Holidays per company guidelines
  • 100% remote setup so you can work wherever you're most productive
  • This role requires meaningful overlap with US Pacific Time business hours
  • Work directly with founders and hiring managers at an early-stage startup with a clear mission
  • Real ownership of how hiring runs, in a company that is growing its team

What You'll Work On

Screening and Sourcing

  • Run preliminary screens for product, design, and go-to-market candidates, and assess fit against the role and the team's hiring bar
  • Do light sourcing and outreach where it helps keep pipelines full, using LinkedIn Recruiter or Juicebox
  • Write clear screen notes and recommendations so hiring managers can decide quickly
  • Keep candidates informed and engaged throughout the process

Hiring Operations and ATS

  • Keep the applicant tracking system accurate and current, including stages, notes, feedback, and dispositions
  • Schedule interviews across candidates and team members and manage the calendar logistics
  • Collect interviewer feedback on time and follow up when it is late
  • Track pipeline status and report on hiring progress to the team

Team Days and Candidate Experience

  • Arrange team days and in-person or virtual interview days, including logistics and communication
  • Make sure each candidate gets a clear, timely, and respectful experience from first contact to decision
  • Support offer and onboarding administration with the team

Process and Improvement

  • Spot where the hiring process is slow or unclear and suggest fixes
  • Help document the process, templates, and standards so hiring scales as the team grows
  • Support the team with research on roles, market, and candidate sources

Requirements

What You Bring

  • Experience recruiting at an early-stage startup, ideally for product management, design, and go-to-market roles
  • Hands-on screening experience and good judgment on candidate quality
  • Hands-on experience with an applicant tracking system and keeping it accurate
  • Experience with LinkedIn Recruiter or Juicebox for sourcing or preliminary screening; existing access to either is a strong plus
  • Strong scheduling and coordination skills across candidates and busy team members
  • Clear writing and professional, warm communication with candidates and hiring managers
  • Organized, dependable, and comfortable working independently in a lean team
  • Comfort using AI tools to speed up research and outreach
  • Available to work full-time with meaningful overlap with US Pacific Time business hours

Nice to Have

  • Experience recruiting for the US market
  • Experience supporting founders as the first or only recruiter
  • Experience recruiting for technology, government, or mission-driven companies
  • Experience organizing team days, on-sites, or candidate events
  • Experience building hiring templates and processes from scratch

How to Apply

Please include:

  1. Your updated resume
  2. A short Loom video (1 to 2 minutes) introducing yourself, describing your startup recruiting experience, and walking through how you would run a 20-minute screen for a product manager candidate and decide whether to advance them

Only candidates who submit a Loom video will be moved to the next step of the hiring process.

If you want to run hiring operations at an early-stage startup, and you take pride in sharp screens, a clean process, and a great candidate experience, this role gives you the ownership and the direct impact to do your best work.

Benefits

Application Process Overview

Our comprehensive selection process ensures we find the right fit for both you and our clients:

  1. Initial Application - Submit your application and complete our prequalifying questions
  2. Video Introduction - Record a video introduction to showcase your communication skills and work experience
  3. Role-Specific Assessment - Complete a homework assignment tailored to the position (if applicable)
  4. Recruitment Interview - Initial screening with our talent team
  5. Executive Interview - Meet with senior leadership to discuss role alignment
  6. Client Interview - Final interview with the client team you'd be supporting
  7. Background & Reference Check - Professional reference verification
  8. Job Offer - Successful candidates receive a formal offer to join the team

Each stage is designed to evaluate your fit for the role while giving you insights into our company culture and expectations. We'll keep you informed throughout the process and provide feedback at each step.

jobs.title: Network Security Engineer
jobs.description:
Misión del rol

Buscamos un/a Network Security Engineer que sea dueño/a de la seguridad de red de Monato en AWS y on-premise. El objetivo es que la infraestructura que procesa pagos B2B esté segmentada, inspeccionada y lista para demostrarlo en cada auditoría.

¿Por qué este rol importa?

Monato está creciendo y su red tiene que crecer con controles. Buscamos un/a Network Security Engineer que se dedique de lleno a la seguridad de red en AWS y on-premise. Su trabajo asegura una red segmentada y auditable ante PCI DSS, SOC 2 e ISO 27001, y permite que Seguridad siga el ritmo que pide el negocio.

Lo que harás

  • Definir y aplicar zonas interna, privada y externa, para que cada servicio quede expuesto solo donde debe y se publique por un camino controlado.
  • Diseñar la segmentación entre cuentas y ambientes de AWS, con Transit Gateway e inspección de tráfico norte-sur y este-oeste.
  • Planear y ejecutar la renovación de los firewalls on-premise, y llevar la visibilidad del data center a nuestro SIEM.
  • Diseñar y probar la segmentación del entorno de tarjetas (CDE), y preparar la evidencia de controles de red para PCI DSS, SOC 2 e ISO 27001.
  • Definir estándares de red como código, con reglas en Terraform que DevOps y Plataforma puedan aplicar sin depender de ti.
  • Detectar y responder a incidentes de red junto con Blue Team, con monitoreo de flujos y alertas en el SIEM.

Perfil y habilidades clave

  • 5+ años de experiencia en seguridad o ingeniería de redes, con al menos 2 diseñando redes en AWS.
  • Experiencia en redes de AWS: VPC, Transit Gateway, PrivateLink, security groups, balanceadores y VPC Flow Logs, con bases sólidas de TCP/IP, DNS, TLS y VPN.
  • Experiencia operando firewalls de nueva generación (Palo Alto, Fortinet u otros) y migrándolos sin cortar la operación.
  • Conocimiento de la segmentación y los controles de red que piden PCI DSS, SOC 2 e ISO 27001, y de cómo se documentan frente a un auditor.
  • Habilidad para definir red y reglas de seguridad como código (Terraform).
  • Capacidad para cambiar redes en producción por olas: modo monitor primero, rollback listo y comunicación con los equipos dueños.
  • Inglés intermedio técnico, para documentación y vendors.
  • Certificación AWS Certified Advanced Networking Specialty o equivalente (nice to have).

Lo que obtendrás

  • Ownership real de la seguridad de red de Monato, desde el diseño hasta la operación.
  • Un rol que se construye desde el inicio: tú defines la estrategia y los estándares de red.
  • Exposición directa a infraestructura de pagos B2B en un entorno regulado.
  • Trabajo cercano con el CISO, DevOps, Plataforma y Blue Team.
  • Crecimiento profesional acelerado dentro de una fintech en etapa de construcción y escala.
  • Cultura de trabajo flexible y enfocada en ejecución.

Acerca de Monato

En Monato construimos infraestructura financiera moderna para empresas en México, integrando servicios financieros de forma ágil y segura. Operamos en un entorno regulado donde la estabilidad y el cumplimiento son fundamentales, y diseñamos soluciones que reducen la fricción bancaria para habilitar el crecimiento de nuestros clientes. Somos un equipo orientado a la ejecución, enfocado en construir, iterar y mejorar constantemente.

jobs.title: Security Analyst
jobs.description:
Security Analyst

Buscamos uma pessoa para assumir um papel de referência técnica em cibersegurança no Grupo, atuando diretamente na proteção dos nossos ambientes, dados, aplicações e operações.

A posição trabalhará em parceria com a Coordenação de Segurança, com foco na operação e evolução técnica da segurança. No dia a dia, será responsável por conectar ferramentas, fornecedores e times internos, ampliando nossa capacidade de identificar vulnerabilidades, antecipar ameaças e responder de forma efetiva a incidentes.

Procuramos alguém com sólida experiência em Blue Team, SecOps e resposta a incidentes, preparado para atuar em um ambiente híbrido e multicloud, com autonomia para investigar riscos, propor melhorias e fortalecer continuamente nossos controles de segurança.

Aqui, buscamos alguém com senso de dono e atuação prática: uma pessoa que questione, investigue e se antecipe aos riscos, contribuindo diretamente para a evolução da maturidade de cibersegurança da empresa.

No dia a dia, você será responsável por:

  • Ser referência técnica no monitoramento de segurança e coordenar tecnicamente a atuação do SOC externo;
  • Receber e aprofundar a investigação de alertas previamente triados, ajustando regras e acompanhando a qualidade das entregas;
  • Garantir uma visão integrada dos diferentes ambientes por meio do SIEM, correlacionando eventos de nuvens, endpoints, colaboração, borda e aplicações;
  • Evoluir regras de detecção e correlação de eventos, fortalecendo continuamente a capacidade de identificação de ameaças;
  • Explorar o potencial das ferramentas de segurança já contratadas e avaliar alternativas quando houver ganho técnico e melhor relação custo-benefício;
  • Garantir níveis consistentes de controles de segurança nos diferentes provedores de nuvem, considerando logs, identidades, workloads e postura de segurança;
  • Liderar tecnicamente a resposta a incidentes, da contenção à análise de causa e lições aprendidas, trabalhando em conjunto com Cloud, Engenharia e fornecedores;
  • Gerenciar vulnerabilidades, apoiando a priorização por risco, acompanhando as correções e controlando os prazos;
  • Mapear a superfície de ataque e identificar ativos com lacunas de proteção, monitoramento ou geração de logs;
  • Integrar e evoluir soluções como WAF, EDR, SIEM, firewall e ferramentas de identidade;
  • Conduzir tecnicamente fornecedores de SOC, MSSP, pentest e demais parceiros de segurança;
  • Definir padrões técnicos de hardening, gestão de segredos e rotação de credenciais, acompanhando sua aderência;
  • Conduzir a segurança no ciclo de desenvolvimento com Engenharia na evolução das práticas de DevSecOps, incluindo SAST, DAST, SCA, segurança de pipelines e APIs;
  • Conduzir tecnicamente pentests de aplicações e infraestrutura, desde a definição do escopo até o acompanhamento da correção dos achados;
  • Incorporar Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) à operação e acompanhar ameaças relevantes ao setor financeiro;
  • Traduzir inteligência de ameaças em regras de detecção e ações de proteção;
  • Realizar e conduzir atividades de threat hunting;
  • Construir e conduzir o roadmap de evolução da maturidade técnica de cibersegurança, priorizando riscos, lacunas de controle e custo-benefício;
  • Avaliar e recomendar soluções de segurança com visão técnica, crítica e financeira;
  • Apoiar ações de cultura de segurança, incluindo simulações de phishing, orientação aos times técnicos e conteúdos baseados em ameaças e incidentes reais;
  • Produzir indicadores e relatórios técnicos sobre a postura de segurança para acompanhamento da Coordenação.

Obrigatórios

Buscamos uma pessoa que tenha:

  • Experiência sólida em cibersegurança operacional, especialmente em Blue Team, SecOps ou resposta a incidentes;
  • Histórico de ter estruturado ou elevado a maturidade de uma operação de segurança, com atuação na evolução de processos, controles e capacidades técnicas;
  • Experiência em liderança técnica de incidentes reais, atuando desde a investigação e contenção até a análise de causa e lições aprendidas;
  • Experiência com SIEM, incluindo criação, manutenção e evolução de regras de detecção e correlação de eventos;
  • Conhecimento prático de detection engineering;
  • Experiência com segurança em nuvem pública e ambientes multicloud em produção;
  • Conhecimentos em segurança de redes, WAF, EDR e DLP;
  • Conhecimento em gestão de endpoints por MDM/UEM;
  • Conhecimento em segurança de identidade, incluindo MFA, acesso condicional e gestão de privilégios;
  • Experiência com segurança de aplicações e práticas de DevSecOps, incluindo SAST, DAST, SCA, segurança de pipelines e APIs;
  • Vivência com CTI e threat hunting;
  • Experiência na condução técnica de fornecedores de segurança, como SOC, MSSP e consultorias de pentest;
  • Capacidade de compreender o negócio, seus processos e dados críticos, direcionando os controles de segurança conforme os riscos;
  • Visão agnóstica de tecnologia, avaliando soluções comerciais e open source de acordo com as necessidades do negócio.

Desejáveis

Será um diferencial se você tiver:

  • Experiência com a stack de segurança Microsoft, especialmente Sentinel/KQL, Defender XDR, Defender for Cloud, Entra ID, Purview e Intune;
  • Vivência em segurança no Google Cloud, incluindo Security Command Center, IAM e Cloud Armor;

Job Description Summary

A dynamic, customer focused individual who has the drive and ability to operate confidently and at times independently, providing operational and maintenance support for the General Electric LM2500 Gas Turbine.
The Coastal Manager (CM) will be a Senior Field Service Representative (FSR), responsible to the Contract Program Manager, whose primary function will be to provide contractual maintenance support to the Royal Canadian Navy West Coast based fleet of LM2500 Gas Turbines. Additionally, the CM will carry out all the responsibilities and perform the job function as the FSR,

Job Description

Job Title

Coastal Manager - West (Senior Field Service Representative, LM2500)


Company Intro/About GE Aerospace

GE Aerospace provides advanced engines, components, and integrated systems that support customers worldwide, including critical defense and marine applications. We partner closely with customers to deliver safe, reliable, and mission-ready outcomes through disciplined execution, strong technical expertise, and responsive support.


Site, Business, OR Functional Area Overview

This role supports GE Aerospace’s marine services work for the Royal Canadian Navy (RCN) on the West Coast of Canada (British Columbia). The Coastal Manager serves as the primary local interface among GE Aerospace, naval ships, the Fleet Maintenance Facility (FMF), and Department of National Defense (DND) operational stakeholders. The role supports sustainment of LM2500 gas turbines through planning and execution of maintenance activities, coordination of supply and spares, and delivery of technical guidance and training.


Role Overview

The Coastal Manager (West) serves as a Senior Field Service Representative (FSR) responsible to the Contract Program Manager. The role provides contractual maintenance and sustainment support for the RCN West Coast-based fleet of LM2500 gas turbines.

In addition to hands-on technical support, this position leads day-to-day coordination across maintenance, logistics, and operations stakeholders, manages spares and repairables, supports subcontractor engagement for specialized requirements, and ensures compliance with GE OEM specifications, safety requirements, and contract obligations.


Key Responsibilities

  • Primary Customer Interface: Serve as the primary point of contact between GE Aerospace, naval ships, FMF personnel, and DND operational management for day-to-day sustainment coordination.
  • Fleet Maintenance Planning: Plan and schedule LM2500 maintenance, repair, and overhaul activities, including coordinating outside subcontractors as required.
  • Level 1/2 Maintenance Execution: Manage and perform LM2500 Level 1 and Level 2 maintenance aboard naval ships and at GE Aerospace coastal facilities, ensuring adherence to OEM technical requirements and safety standards.
  • Engineering & Technical Liaison: Provide technical liaison between ships, DND/FM F stakeholders, and GE Aerospace resources; communicate technical findings, recommendations, and follow-up actions.
  • Spares & Inventory Management: Manage spares and materials for the West Coast scope, including forecasting, control, procurement support, inventory reporting, and material readiness.
  • Repairable Item (RI) Process Ownership: Coordinate the RI flow end-to-end: receipt of removed items, routing through repair processes, and return to inventory.
  • Component Repair / Vendor Management: Manage subcontractor and vendor relationships for component repair, including performance follow-up and schedule adherence.
  • Engine Life Management & Tracking: Track engine life and configuration data to support readiness decisions and sustainment planning.
  • Customer Training Delivery: Provide classroom and practical LM2500 training to customer personnel as required; support skills transfer and standardization of maintenance practices.
  • Mentoring & Team Support: Serve as a mentor/trainer for less experienced GE Aerospace marine FSRs and support technical development of customer staff as needed.
  • Program Updates & Risk Management: Lead regular internal program updates; analyze contract operational risks and drive corrective actions to protect delivery and readiness objectives.

Required Qualifications

  • Experience: Minimum 5 years of experience (within the last 7 years) specializing in marine propulsion or power generation field service, specifically on GE LM model gas turbines
  • Supervisory Experience: Minimum 2 years of maintenance supervisory experience (within the last 5 years) focused on gas turbine applications
  • Tools: Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint)
  • License: Valid driver’s license
  • On-Call Availability: Ability to participate in on-call support as required
  • Schedule Flexibility / Travel: Ability to support occasional domestic/international travel, overtime, and weekend work as needed
  • Security: Must possess a Government of Canada Secret Level Security Clearance or have the ability to obtain and maintain such clearance (mandatory)
  • Clearance Level: Level II (Secret) clearance required

Additional Information

  • Pay Range (BC, Canada): The pay range for this position is $104,600.00 - $130,800.00 CAD annual. The specific pay offered may be influenced by a variety of factors, including the candidate’s experience, education, and skill set.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience supporting military operations or defense customers, including naval environments
  • Strong oral communication and technical writing skills
  • Ability to communicate effectively with internal and external stakeholders, including senior leadership
  • Strong interpersonal and collaboration skills in cross-functional environments
  • Ability to coordinate multiple projects simultaneously

Closing

At GE Aerospace, we are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace that values diversity and empowers employees to thrive. This role may require access to export-controlled information and/or government-controlled data. Where applicable, final offers will be contingent on the ability to obtain authorization for such access from the appropriate government authorities.

jobs.title: Staff Security Engineer
jobs.description:
The Mill Adventure is a scale-up with the ultimate mission of building awesome products that will change the way the iGaming industry operates. We started our journey in 2019 with the vision of building a technology-driven organisation and creating a team consisting of the best of the best specialists in their respective fields.

Today, we provide a complete gaming platform for rapid deployment and success in iGaming. Our team of 100+ technology and iGaming experts is guided by a passion for invention, operational excellence and commitment to improving the inefficient.

We trust and value our team and strive to accommodate the right working conditions for each individual in remote, office-based or mixed models. We see the strength in being different and embracing the cultural diversity existing in our group.

One of our key strengths is our modern, event-driven, serverless technology stack, which allows us to innovate and move fast. We work in a collaborative environment that values both teamwork and autonomy.

The Role
As a Staff Security Engineer, you will be the cornerstone of our product and cloud security posture. You will own security across the code, the cloud, the pipelines, the corporate estate, and the response when an alert comes in.

This is a hands-on role with real architectural ownership. You will design our security controls and then build them — our security team is small, and you will be one of three people, so there is nobody to hand a design to. That cuts both ways: almost nothing stands between a good idea and it being live, and there is nowhere to hide if it doesn't get delivered. If your recent work has been mostly programme management, vendor oversight or reviewing other people's designs, this won't be the right fit.

Much of the work will also happen through other people. Security can't do everything alone, so you will spend real time with developers and architects — reviewing designs, threat modelling, coaching on secure practices — and your impact will be measured as much by what they build securely as by what you build yourself.

The role spans security engineering, IT security, security operations and a degree of offensive security. Breadth matters less as a checklist than as judgement: knowing which risks are real, which findings are noise, what to fix first, and — most importantly — what to automate so it stays fixed without anyone watching it.

You will be doing this in 2026, which means AI sits on both sides of the board. Attackers move faster and cheaper than they did two years ago, and the only realistic way for three people to cover this surface is to build AI into how the team works. You should already be doing this, not planning to.

On how we work: we review each other's work openly, and designs get challenged on their merits. We think that produces better security, and we'd expect you to challenge ours in the same way.

What You'll Do:

  • Architect and lead the design and implementation of security controls across our cloud infrastructure, applications and CI/CD pipelines — and build them yourself
  • Coach and mentor developers, engineers and architects on secure design, threat modelling and cloud security, so that security scales beyond the security team and becomes part of how we build
  • Own vulnerability management and our attack surface: know what is exposed, prioritise by real exploitability rather than scanner severity, and drive findings to closure with the teams that own them
  • Own the security of the SDLC by integrating and tuning SAST, DAST and SCA so that developers keep them enabled because the signal is worth the friction
  • Engineer and maintain our cloud security posture, primarily in AWS and Cloudflare — hardening configurations, automating compliance checks, and closing gaps before they are found for you
  • Own detection and response end to end: shape what we log and alert on, tune out the noise, investigate what is real, remediate it, and write up what happened
  • Architect and guide our IAM strategy, working with engineering to deliver least-privilege access for human and machine identities that teams don't route around
  • Test our own systems. Use offensive techniques against our infrastructure, applications and identity flows to validate that controls work and to decide what actually gets fixed first
  • Use AI as a force multiplier for a team that is small relative to its surface — agentic tooling for triage, code review, detection engineering, evidence collection and the automation of toil. You will also be the person who secures AI systems as we adopt them
  • Automate everything. If you would otherwise do it twice, automate it
  • Bring us the uncomfortable assessments — with a plan and a first PR attached

Requirements

  • 5+ years hands-on in a technical security engineering role, including time where you were the person accountable for the fix, not the person who raised the ticket. Expect to be asked what you built, what it prevented, and how you knew it worked
  • You design and you deliver. You can produce an architecture that survives review, and you have a track record of the things you designed actually going live
  • Judgement across security engineering, IT security, security operations and offensive security. We are not looking for equal depth in all four — we are looking for someone who can tell a real risk from a noisy one across all of them, and who automates the response rather than handling it manually each time
  • Deep AWS security: IAM, Organizations and SCPs, Security Hub, GuardDuty, WAF, plus Cloudflare. You can walk through how you would detect and contain a compromised role, not just describe what each service does
  • You write code that runs in production and that other people depend on — Python, Go, Bash, with TypeScript a major plus
  • Infrastructure as Code and its real failure modes: drift, over-permissive modules, secrets in state, pipeline privilege escalation
  • Vulnerability and attack surface management you have personally run — including the harder half, which is getting other teams to close things
  • Solid understanding of SIEM and detection engineering: what to collect, how to turn it into detections that fire on real activity, and how to keep false positives from burying the team
  • Detection and response you have personally done. You have investigated real alerts and written the post-incident review
  • Working offensive knowledge. You need not be a pentester, but you should be able to chain misconfigurations into a real attack path and explain why one finding matters more than fifty from a scanner
  • Practical use of AI in your security work today, not curiosity about it. Tell us what you have built or automated with it, where it failed you, and how you validate what it produces
  • A current, specific view on AI-driven threats — what has actually changed for defenders, and what you would do about it here
  • SDLC security: SAST, DAST and SCA that you have integrated and, more importantly, tuned well enough that developers didn't turn them off
  • The ability to work autonomously without going dark, and to work closely with engineers without friction. Both, not one
  • Comfort with open technical debate. You can have a design challenged in review, make your case, and move forward either way

Nice to have:

  • Hands-on experience with PCI DSS — scoping, control implementation and evidence — as something you have engineered towards, not only been audited against.
  • Experience building and maintaining a SIEM: pipelines, parsing, cost control, detection-as-code.
  • Serverless and event-driven architecture at scale.
  • iGaming, fintech or another regulated, high-value-target industry.
  • Corporate IT security: SSO and identity providers, MDM, SaaS security posture, third-party and vendor access.
  • Experience securing AI or agentic systems.
  • Security frameworks (NIST CSF, CIS Benchmarks, CSA CCM) used as tools to get work done rather than as the work itself.
  • Public artifacts: tools you have released, writeups, CVEs, CTF results, talks.
  • Certifications such as CISSP, AWS Certified Security or CEH are welcome, though demonstrated work weighs considerably more in our process

Benefits

  • A lean, focused company, offering a flexible working environment
  • The opportunity to work with and learn form a highly skilled, talented team
  • A great company culture, where accountability is innate, transparency is key and competency is virtue
  • Being part of a tight knit, caring community
  • Work equipment of your choice
  • Private health insurance
  • Learning budget
  • Company wide and team based get togethers

  • Apoiar a operacionalização de ferramentas e integrações de garantia contínua, em parceria com Engenharia de IAM nas frentes de acesso a dados, automação, testes e preparação para produção.
  • Definir e manter o fluxo da detecção à remediação, incluindo avaliação de riscos, atribuição de responsáveis, investigação, acompanhamento da remediação, validação, escalonamento e retenção de evidências.
  • Investigar constatações e exceções recorrentes, identificar causas-raiz e trabalhar com os responsáveis por controles e tecnologia para definir ações corretivas viáveis e acompanhá-las até a conclusão.
  • Produzir indicadores claros de eficácia dos controles, relatórios de exceções, painéis e evidências prontas para auditoria, ajudando as partes interessadas a compreender a exposição e agir.
  • Contribuir para procedimentos de garantia, documentação técnica, manuais operacionais e transferência de conhecimento, para que a equipe de IAM possa manter o monitoramento de forma consistente.
  • Coordenar atividades de garantia com Auditoria Interna, Riscos e Compliance, mantendo responsabilidades claras e o nível adequado de independência.

Como o sucesso será medido

  • Os controles prioritários de IGA e PAM são monitorados por verificações repetíveis e baseadas em riscos, com maior cobertura de sistemas críticos e acessos de alto risco.
  • Problemas acionáveis nos controles de IAM são identificados precocemente, atribuídos a responsáveis e acompanhados até a remediação e validação, dentro dos prazos acordados.
  • Exceções em revisões de acesso, riscos de acesso privilegiado, contas órfãs e exceções a políticas são tratadas por fluxos documentados, com evidências rastreáveis.
  • A eficácia dos controles e as tendências de exceções são reportadas de forma consistente, e as solicitações de auditoria são atendidas com evidências completas e confiáveis.
  • Com o tempo, os processos de monitoramento e garantia tornam-se mais automatizados e menos dependentes da coleta manual de evidências.
  • A documentação, os manuais operacionais e as transições para a operação permitem que a equipe de IAM mantenha as capacidades implementadas.

Experiência e qualificações

Você tem experiência comprovada em IAM, controles de segurança, garantia, riscos de TI ou área relacionada e consegue atuar diretamente com dados de identidade e acesso, responsáveis por controles e equipes técnicas.

  • Experiência na análise de dados de acesso para identificar exceções, tendências, fragilidades de controle ou riscos potenciais e transformar constatações em ações corretivas viáveis.
  • Conhecimento prático dos conceitos e objetivos de controle de IGA e PAM, incluindo privilégio mínimo, governança de contas privilegiadas e processos de revisão de acesso.

jobs.title: Clinical Trial Manager
jobs.description:
Noah Labs is a digital cardiology start-up, based in Berlin and Boston. We already run a CE-marked remote patient monitoring platform deployed across Europe, and we’re now developing Noah Labs Vox, a voice-based Software as a Medical Device that detects worsening heart failure from short daily smartphone recordings.

Vox holds FDA Breakthrough Device Designation, with our FDA pivotal trial underway across 15+ sites in the US, Canada and Europe. We partner with leading academic centers and health systems across Europe and the US, including Charité, the Mayo Clinic, Duke, and Harvard.

Everything we do is anchored in one goal: helping patients with heart failure live longer, healthier lives.

Tasks

The role

As Vox is now gaining traction and momentum in the US, you will own the operational execution of our US clinical program - the FDA pivotal trial (15+ sites, De Novo submission) and a randomized pragmatic trial embedded in routine care, as well as oversight of our European MDR investigations run out of Berlin.

We don't work with a full-service CRO. This means you're not managing a vendor relationship, you're building the function itself, the one Noah Labs scales on after clearance. You'll manage sites directly, coordinate the academic partners and specialist vendors who provide independent trial functions, and help grow the clinical team as we go. You work directly with our CMedO, Clinical Research Lead, regulatory, product and R&D. You report directly to our CMedO and work face-to-face with investigators at leading US cardiology centers and inside the FDA dialogue that's shaping what a new device category even looks like.

If you like to bring structure to ambiguity and are comfortable making decisions amid uncertainty, this role is built for you.

In this role you will

  • Lead trial start-up including site selection, agreements, and budgets, IRB submissions, site initiation and training
  • Drive enrollment and protocol adherence across sites in close partnership with investigators and site coordinators
  • Own the monitoring strategy and personally conduct monitoring visits, both remote and on-site, in addition to managing any contract monitors
  • Own study budgets, timelines and risk registers, reporting directly to the Chief Medical Officer
  • Run the operational backbone: eTMF, EDC, data cleaning, and protocol deviations
  • Ensure audit and inspection readiness (FDA BIMO, IRB) and maintain sponsor SOPs’
  • Support the European investigations and regulatory compliance (ISO 14155, MDR)
  • Author and maintain SOPs and work instructions (WIs) for clinical operations, monitoring, and data management

Requirements

What we're looking for

  • Degree in life sciences, nursing, medicine, biomedical engineering or a related field
  • 5+ years in clinical research, including 3+ years in US FDA-regulated devices
  • Familiarity with SaMD clinical trials
  • Hands-on experience with the full IRB submission lifecycle: preparing and submitting packages, then amending documents like the CIP and ICF as the protocol changes.
  • Hands-on experience taking a US multicenter trial from start-up through enrollment, and closing, on the sponsor side and without a full-service CRO
  • Working knowledge of 21 CFR Parts 812, 50, 56 and 11, ICH-GCP, ISO 14155 and HIPAA; practical experience with EDC and eTMF systems
  • Structured problem-solving and clear prioritization under shifting timelines
  • Strong stakeholder management across academic sites, health systems and senior KOLs
  • Uncompromising on patient safety, data integrity and inspection readiness
  • Fluency in English
  • Authorized to work in the US

Nice to have

  • Cardiology or heart failure trials; pragmatic or health-system-embedded trials.
  • App-based or remote monitoring studies (patient onboarding, adherence, technical support)
  • Contribution to a De Novo, 510(k) or PMA clinical evidence package
  • Advanced academic degree (e.g. MSc)

Things to be aware of

This is a remote, US-based role with regular presence at study sites – up to 30% travel in the first 12 months, less thereafter, plus occasional trips to our Berlin office. Working hours bridge US and Berlin time zones.

Benefits

💵$90–150K depending on experience, plus meaningful equity

🫀Bring a first-in-class digital biomarker through FDA clearance and into routine care

🚀 A dynamic startup with exceptional talent from Harvard, TUM, Meta and Stanford

🌎 Fully remote setup in the US with regular visits to our Berlin headquarters

✈️ Direct exposure to leading US cardiology centers and the FDA Breakthrough Devices process

Apply Now and be a part of our mission to transform heart failure management through cutting-edge technology and compassionate care.

jobs.title: Care Team Intake Specialist
jobs.description:
About Synapticure

Synapticure is the largest, most comprehensive specialty care and life sciences company in the country for those living with neurodegenerative diseases. Founded by patients and caregivers living with these diseases, we are redefining the care and the research paradigm for conditions like Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and ALS in all 50 states.

Our business is powered by two connected engines.

The CARES Engine (Clinical Operations)

A scalable, 50-state virtualized clinical network providing timely access to expert neurologists and cutting edge treatments with wraparound care coordination and behavioral health support. Our team creates personalized care plans focused on education and empowerment, connecting patients with a multidisciplinary team of subspecialty neurologists, geriatricians, psychologists, and care coordinators who collaborate to deliver comprehensive care.

The CURES Engine (Research & Innovation)

Leveraging our deeply engaged, well characterized national patient cohort, CURES partners with life science, pharma, biotech, and medical device companies to accelerate the development of neurodegenerative treatments, spanning discovery stage lab services, clinical trial services, and real world evidence data and analytics.

Partnering with providers, health plans, and life sciences companies, including CMS' GUIDE dementia care model, Synapticure is dedicated to transforming the lives of millions of individuals and their families living with neurodegenerative diseases.

About the Role

    Synapticure is dedicated to ensuring all individuals living with neurodegenerative diseases have equitable access to the highest standard of care while fueling the advancement of personalized treatments. We create a guided, compassionate journey for every patient, caregiver, and family, educating and empowering them while facilitating access to critical tests and leading specialists across the United States.

    As a Care Team Intake Specialist, you will be the welcoming first point of contact for members, caregivers, and loved ones navigating neurodegenerative conditions. You will drive essential clinical and administrative support functions, including scheduling, registration, referrals, and prior authorizations, serving as a trusted representative of Synapticure to our members, external healthcare organizations, and payer partners.

    This is an opportunity to make a meaningful, daily impact on people's lives within a mission-driven, rapidly evolving environment. We are looking for an empathetic, curious, and organized communicator who thrives in collaborative spaces and is committed to delivering respectful, culturally responsive, and accessible care to diverse communities.

The Day to Day

    Member Engagement & Care Coordination

  • Conduct welcoming, empathetic intake calls with new patients and caregivers to gather medical histories, current and past provider details, and insurance information.
  • Schedule, confirm, and manage clinical appointments across virtual platforms, ensuring daily scheduling benchmarks and protocols are met.
  • Proactively manage cancellations, rescheduling requests, and appointment reminders via phone, video, and digital communication tools.
  • Collaborate closely with the multidisciplinary care team to coordinate care, complete visit-related tasks, and execute FMLA forms.
  • Advocate on behalf of patients and families with clinical providers, billing departments, and insurance partners while maintaining strict adherence to HIPAA guidelines.

    • Operations, Documentation & Follow-Up

  • Request, collect, and audit external medical records, member consents, and HIPAA forms to ensure care teams have complete information prior to appointments.
  • Conduct insurance eligibility checks and assist with prior authorizations and referral management.
  • Accurately document member clinical and demographic data, calls, and correspondence in our Electronic Health Record (EHR) and care facilitation platforms in a timely manner.
  • Manage incoming and outgoing communications, including faxes, digital messages, and mailed member resources.
  • Follow standardized operating procedures and quality assurance protocols while remaining adaptable to evolving workflows and priorities.
  • Generate standard operational reports and support additional care team initiatives as needed.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 1-2+ years of experience in patient communication, care coordination, medical scheduling, or managing referrals and prior authorizations.
  • Comfort with digital communication tools, telehealth platforms, Electronic Health Record (EHR) systems, and standard office technology.
  • Working knowledge of HIPAA privacy guidelines and handling confidential medical records.
  • Strong active listening skills and the ability to communicate clearly, patiently, and non-judgmentally with individuals from diverse backgrounds and varying accessibility needs.
  • Ability to stay organized, prioritize tasks effectively, and adapt in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 3+ years of experience in a healthcare setting, such as a Medical Assistant (MA), Patient Care Coordinator, Medical Records Specialist, or similar clinical/administrative support role.
  • Familiarity with healthcare operations, medical terminology, FMLA documentation, and frequently prescribed medications.
  • Experience requesting, reviewing, and auditing external medical records for completeness and accuracy.
  • Hands-on proficiency with cloud-based EHR systems (e.g., Epic, Athenahealth, eClinicalWorks), macOS, and Google Workspace.
  • Experience working in a remote setting, startup, or mission-driven organization undergoing rapid growth and change.

Schedule

    We are looking for candidates who are flexible to work the below schedule, based on your time zone, Monday through Friday.

  • Pacific: 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM PT
  • Mountain: 9:00 AM to 5:30 PM MT
  • Central: 10:00 AM to 6:30 PM CT
  • Eastern: 11:00 AM to 7:30 PM ET

Compensation

Final compensation will be determined based on location, experience, and qualifications.

Our Values

We are a remote-first company. While our team is located all across the United States, these core principles tie us together around a common identity:

  • Relentless focus on patients and caregivers: We are determined to provide an exceptional experience for every patient we have the privilege to serve, and we put our patients first in everything we do.
  • Embody the spirit and humanity of those living with neurodegenerative disease: Inspired by our founders, families, and personal experiences, we recognize the seriousness of our patients' circumstances and meet that challenge every day with empathy, compassion, kindness, joy, and hope.
  • Seek to understand, and stay curious: We start by listening to one another, our partners, our patients, and their caregivers. We communicate with authenticity and humility, prioritizing honesty and directness while recognizing we always have something to learn.
  • Embrace the opportunity: We are energized by the importance of our mission and maintain a strong bias toward action.

Benefits & Perks

Full time employees are eligible for:

  • Remote First: Work from anywhere in the 50 United States, with home office technology provided.
  • Comprehensive Healthcare: Medical, dental, and vision insurance options for you and your family.
  • Financial & Retirement Support: 401(k) plan with employer matching, plus short and long-term disability, and basic and supplemental life insurance.
  • Time Off & Leave: 15 vacation days, 5 sick days, 12 paid holidays, and 2 floating holidays, plus a fully paid end-of-year company holiday break (typically Christmas through New Year's).
  • Wellness & Family Growth: Comprehensive family-building and fertility services through Kindbody (where available) at a 20% discount, 24/7 mental health support via Health Advocate and Talkspace (including 12 free on-demand sessions per year), and access to One Medical.

Travel Requirements & Remote Workplace Setup

We're a remote-first company and provide the necessary technology to work from home. Most roles involve only occasional travel, such as for team meetings or professional collaboration events, unless otherwise specified in the job-specific details above.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Synapticure is an equal opportunity employer and a remote-first workplace. We believe that embedding equity, inclusion, compliance, and operational excellence across all aspects of our employee lifecycle directly reflects our core values. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Please apply even if you feel you do not meet all qualifications.

At this time, Synapticure is unable to provide work visa sponsorship.

If you require reasonable accommodation in completing this application, interviewing, completing any pre-employment testing, or otherwise participating in the employee selection process, please direct your inquiries to .
